title.zh: 卷四十二 蜀書十二 杜周杜許孟來尹李譙郤傳
title.en: Volume 42: Book of Shu 12 - Biographies of Du, Zhou, Du, Xu, Meng, Lai, Yin, Li, Qiao, and Xi
title.raw: 卷四十二 蜀書十二 杜周杜許孟來尹李譙郤傳 Volume 42: Book of Shu 12 - Biographies of Du, Zhou, Du, Xu, Meng, Lai, Yin, Li, Qiao, and Xi

sentences.zh: 杜微字國輔，梓潼涪人也。

translations.literal: Du Wei, courtesy name Guofu, was a man of Fu in Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei, styled Guofu, came from Fu in Zitong commandery.

sentences.zh: 少受學於廣漢任安。

translations.literal: In youth he received learning from Ren An of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Ren An of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 劉障辟為從事，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang summoned him as staff aide; because of illness he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang appointed him a staff aide, but he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 及先主定蜀，微常稱聾，閉門不出。

translations.literal: When the First Sovereign settled Shu, Wei constantly claimed deafness, closed the gate and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took Shu, Du Wei feigned deafness and shut himself away.

sentences.zh: 建興二年，丞相亮領益州牧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianxing, Chancellor Liang led Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 224 Zhuge Liang became governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 選迎皆妙簡舊德，以秦宓為別駕，五梁為功曹，微為主簿。

translations.literal: In selection and welcome all were subtly chosen from old virtue, appointing Qin Mi as aide-de-camp, Wu Liang as merit clerk, Wei as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His appointments favored established worthies: Qin Mi as aide-de-camp, Wu Liang as merit clerk, and Du Wei as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 微固辭，舉而致之。

translations.literal: Wei firmly declined; they raised him and brought him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei refused firmly, so they had him carried to office.

sentences.zh: 既致，亮引見微，微自陳謝。

translations.literal: Once brought, Liang led audience with Wei; Wei personally stated thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Zhuge Liang received him; Du Wei apologized for his reluctance.

sentences.zh: 亮以微不聞人語，於坐上與書曰：

translations.literal: Liang because Wei did not hear people's speech, on the seat wrote him saying:
translations.idiomatic: Because Du Wei could not hear speech, Zhuge Liang wrote to him at their meeting:

sentences.zh: 服聞德行，飢渴歷時，清濁異流，無緣諮覯。

translations.literal: Having heard of virtue and conduct, hunger and thirst through seasons, clear and muddy different streams, without fate to consult and meet.
translations.idiomatic: I have long admired your virtue from afar, yet as clear stays apart from muddy water we have never met.

sentences.zh: 王元泰、李伯仁、王文儀、楊季休、丁君乾、李永南兄弟、文仲寶等，每歎高志，未見如舊。

translations.literal: Wang Yuantai, Li Boren, Wang Wenyi, Yang Jixiu, Ding Junqian, Li Yongnan and brothers, Wen Zhongbao and others, each sighed at lofty aims, not seeing as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuantai, Li Shao, Wang Wenyi, Yang Hong, Ding Gong, the Li brothers Yongnan, Wen Zhongbao, and the rest often speak of your high purpose; they miss you as in former days.

sentences.zh: 猥以空虛，統領貴州，德薄任重，慘慘憂慮、朝廷主公今年始十八，天姿仁敏，愛德下士。

translations.literal: Vulgarly with emptiness, leading and governing your noble province, virtue thin burden heavy, deeply anxious—the court's lord this year only eighteen, heaven-given nature humane and keen, loving virtue and lowering himself to gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy yet hold this province; my virtue is slight and my burden heavy, and I worry constantly. Our sovereign in the capital has just turned eighteen: humane, quick of mind, and eager to honor good men.

sentences.zh: 天下之人思慕漢室，欲與君因天順民，輔此明主，以隆季興之功，著勳於竹帛也。

translations.literal: The people of the realm think longingly of the Han house, wishing with you to follow heaven and accord with the people, aid this enlightened ruler, thereby to magnify the merit of restoring the season's rise, inscribe achievement on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: All who long for the house of Han wish you would heed Heaven and the people, support this enlightened ruler, enlarge the work of restoring the dynasty, and leave your name on the record.

sentences.zh: 以謂賢愚下相為謀，故自割絕，守勞而已，不圖自屈也。

translations.literal: Deeming worthy and foolish below mutually to scheme, therefore self-cut off, guarding toil only, did not plan self to bend.
translations.idiomatic: You thought wise and simple could not counsel together, so you cut yourself off and kept to your quiet life—I never thought you would humble yourself to come.

sentences.zh: 微自乞老病求歸，亮又與書答曰：

translations.literal: Wei himself begged old age and illness seeking return; Liang again wrote answering saying:
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei asked to retire on account of age and infirmity; Zhuge Liang wrote again:

sentences.zh: 曹丕篡弒，自立為帝，是猶土龍芻狗之有名也。

translations.literal: Cao Pi usurped and murdered, established himself as emperor—this is still like an earthen dragon and straw dog having a name.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi murdered his liege and seized the throne—a thing as empty as a clay dragon or a straw dog parading a title.

sentences.zh: 欲與羣賢因其邪偽，以正道滅之。

translations.literal: I wish with the host of worthies to follow his perverse falsehood, with correct way to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to join the worthy in turning his own treachery against him and destroy him by right.

sentences.zh: 怪君未有相誨，便欲求還於山野。

translations.literal: I marvel, sir, you have not yet mutually instructed, then wish to seek return in mountain wilds.
translations.idiomatic: I am surprised you offer no counsel yet already wish to flee to the hills.

sentences.zh: 丕又大興勞役，以向吳、楚。

translations.literal: Pi again greatly raised labor corvée, to advance on Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi is again driving his people on vast corvées against Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 今因丕多務，且以閉境勤農，育養民物，並治甲兵，以待其挫，然後伐之，可使兵不戰民不勞而天下定也。

translations.literal: Now because Pi has many tasks, for the nonce close borders and diligently farm, nurture and rear the people and things, together manage armor and weapons, to await his setback, then afterward strike him—can cause troops not to fight, people not to toil, yet the realm to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: While he is overbusy, we should seal the borders, encourage farming, rest the people, and ready arms until he falters—then strike so that the realm may be settled without needless battles or wear on the folk.

sentences.zh: 君但當以德輔時耳，不責君軍事，何為汲汲欲求去乎！

translations.literal: Sir only ought with virtue to aid the times; I do not demand of you military affairs—why urgently urgently wish to seek to leave!
translations.idiomatic: You need only lend your virtue to the times; I do not press you for military duty—why this haste to withdraw?

sentences.zh: 其敬微如此，拜為諫議大夫，以從其志。

translations.literal: His respect for Wei was thus; appointed grandee remonstrant, thereby to follow his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Zhuge Liang’s deference to him: he named him grandee remonstrant to suit his wish to serve without heavy burden.

sentences.zh: 五梁者，字德山，犍為南安人也，以儒學節操稱。

translations.literal: As for Wu Liang, courtesy name Deshan, a man of Nan'an in Qianwei, by Confucian learning and integrity he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Liang, styled Deshan, of Nan'an in Qianwei, was known for classical learning and upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 從議郎遷諫義大夫、五官中朗將。

translations.literal: From gentleman consultant was promoted remonstrance grandee, general of the household for all purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from gentleman consultant to remonstrance grandee and general of the household for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 周羣字仲直，巴西閬中人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Qun, courtesy name Zhongzhi, was a man of Langzhong in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qun, styled Zhongzhi, came from Langzhong in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 父舒，字叔布，少學術於廣漢楊厚，名亞董扶、任安。

translations.literal: Father Shu, courtesy name Shubu, in youth studied arts from Yang Hou of Guanghan; fame was next below Dong Fu and Ren An.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhou Shu, styled Shubu, studied occult arts under Yang Hou of Guanghan and ranked just below Dong Fu and Ren An in renown.

sentences.zh: 數被徵，終不詣。

translations.literal: Several times was summoned; in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned repeatedly but never went.

sentences.zh: 時人有問：「《春秋讖》曰『代漢者當塗高』，此何謂也？

translations.literal: Someone of the time asked: "The Spring and Autumn prophecy says 'He who replaces Han will be dangtu gao'—what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him what the Spring and Autumn prophecy meant by “he who replaces Han will be dangtu gao.”

sentences.zh: 」舒曰：「當塗高者，魏也。

translations.literal: " Shu said, "Dangtu gao is Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shu answered that “dangtu gao” meant Wei.

sentences.zh: 」鄉黨學者私傳其語，羣少受學於舒，專心候業。

translations.literal: " Village and district scholars privately passed his words; Qun in youth received learning from Shu, single-mindedly devoted to prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: Village scholars repeated his words in private. Zhou Qun studied under his father and devoted himself to celestial observation.

sentences.zh: 於庭中做小樓，家富多奴，常令奴更直於樓上視天災，才見一氣，即白羣，羣自上樓觀之，不避晨夜，故凡有氣候，無不見之者，是以所言多中。

translations.literal: In the courtyard he built a small tower; the family was rich with many slaves; constantly ordered slaves in rotation on duty on the tower to watch heaven's calamities; as soon as one saw one qi, then reported to Qun; Qun himself ascended the tower to observe, not avoiding dawn or night; therefore whenever there was weather-sign, none he did not see—therefore what he spoke mostly hit.
translations.idiomatic: He built a small tower in his courtyard and, being wealthy, set slaves in shifts on its roof to watch the sky. At the first trace of an omen they called Zhou Qun, who climbed up day or night to look himself, so he missed no portent and his predictions usually proved true.

sentences.zh: 州牧劉璋辟以為師友從事。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Zhang summoned him as mentor-and-friend aide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang named him mentor-and-friend on his staff.

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢書》曰：建安七年，越巂有男子化為女人，時羣言哀帝時亦有此，將易代之祥也。

translations.literal: 〈The Xu Han shu states: In the seventh year of Jian'an, in Yuexi there was a man who transformed into a woman; at the time Qun said in Emperor Ai's time there was also this—it will be an omen of changing the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Han shu records that in 202 a man in Yuexi turned into a woman; Zhou Qun said the same had happened under Emperor Ai of Han and foretold a change of dynasty.

sentences.zh: 至二十五年，獻帝果封於山陽。

translations.literal: Reaching the twenty-fifth year, the Emperor Xian indeed was enfeoffed at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 220 the emperor was indeed enfeoffed at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，有星孛於鶉尾，荊州分野，羣以為荊州牧將死而失土。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year, there was a broom star in the Quail's Tail, Jing Province's field division; Qun thought the Governor of Jing would die and lose land.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 207 a comet appeared in the Quail’s Tail, Jingzhou’s celestial field; Zhou Qun predicted the Jing governor would die and lose his territory.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，劉表卒，曹公平荊州。

translations.literal: The next year autumn, Liu Biao died, Lord Cao pacified Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn Liu Biao died and Cao Cao took Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年十二月，星孛於五諸侯，羣以為西方專據土地者皆將失土。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year, a broom star at the Five Feudatories; Qun thought those who monopolized holding land in the west would all lose land.
translations.idiomatic: In December 212 a comet appeared at the Five Feudatories; Zhou Qun said every western warlord who held territory would lose it.

sentences.zh: 是時，劉璋據益州，張魯據漢中，韓遂據涼州，宋建據枹罕。

translations.literal: At this time Liu Zhang held Yizhou, Zhang Lu held Hanzhong, Han Sui held Liangzhou, Song Jian held Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zhang held Yizhou, Zhang Lu Hanzhong, Han Sui Liangzhou, and Song Jian Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，曹公遣偏將擊涼州。

translations.literal: The next year winter, Lord Cao sent a detached general to strike Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter Cao Cao sent a column against Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年，獲宋建，韓遂逃於羌中，被殺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, captured Song Jian; Han Sui fled among the Qiang and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In 214 Song Jian was captured, Han Sui fled among the Qiang and was killed.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，璋失益州。

translations.literal: That year autumn, Zhang lost Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Liu Zhang lost Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年秋，曹公攻漢中，張魯降。〉

translations.literal: In the twentieth year autumn, Lord Cao attacked Hanzhong, Zhang Lu surrendered.〉
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 215 Cao Cao attacked Hanzhong and Zhang Lu surrendered.〉

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，署儒林校尉。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu, appointed him Colonel of the Forest of Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took Shu he named him colonel of the forest of scholars.

sentences.zh: 先主欲曹公爭漢中，問羣，羣對曰：「當得其地，不得其民也，若出偏軍，必不利，當戒慎之！

translations.literal: The First Sovereign wished to contend with Lord Cao for Hanzhong, asked Qun; Qun replied saying, "You ought to obtain its land, not obtain its people; if you send a detached army, certainly it will not be favorable—you ought to guard and be careful!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei planned to contest Hanzhong with Cao Cao, he asked Zhou Qun, who said he would take the ground but not the people, and warned that a detached column would fare badly.

sentences.zh: 」時州後部司馬蜀郡張裕亦曉佔候，而天才過羣，

translations.literal: " At the time rear-division major of the province Zhang Yu of Shu commandery also understood divination by observation, yet heaven's talent surpassed Qun,
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu of Shu, rear-division major of the province, also practiced astrology and was even more gifted than Zhou Qun.

sentences.zh: 〈裕字南和。〉

translations.literal: 〈Yu's courtesy name Nanhe.〉
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy name was Nanhe.〉

sentences.zh: 諫先主曰：「不可爭漢中，軍必不利。

translations.literal: He remonstrated the First Sovereign saying, "You cannot contest Hanzhong—the army certainly will not be favorable."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Liu Bei not to fight for Hanzhong, saying the army would meet disaster.

sentences.zh: 」先主竟不用裕言，果得地而不得民也。

translations.literal: " The First Sovereign in the end did not use Yu's words; indeed obtained land but did not obtain people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei ignored Zhang Yu and indeed took the land without winning the people.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍吳蘭、雷銅等入成都，皆沒不還，悉如羣言。

translations.literal: He sent Generals Wu Lan, Lei Tong, and others to enter Chengdu; all were lost and did not return—entirely as Qun had said.
translations.idiomatic: The generals Wu Lan, Lei Tong, and others whom he sent toward Chengdu were destroyed to a man, just as Zhou Qun had foretold.

sentences.zh: 於是舉羣茂才。

translations.literal: Thereupon raised Qun as flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qun was then nominated flourishing talent.

sentences.zh: 裕又私語人曰：「歲在庚子，天下當易代，劉氏祚盡矣。

translations.literal: Yu again privately told someone saying, "When the year stands in gengzi, the realm ought to change the age; the Liu house's fate is exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu also whispered that in the gengzi year the mandate would change and the house of Liu would end.

sentences.zh: 主公得益州，九年之後，寅卯之間當失之。

translations.literal: When the lord obtained Yizhou, after nine years, between yin and mao he ought to lose it.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years after the lord took Yizhou he would lose it in the yin or mao year.

sentences.zh: 」入密白其言。

translations.literal: " Someone entered and secretly reported his words.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported his words in secret.

sentences.zh: 初，先主與劉璋會涪，時裕為璋從事，侍坐，其人饒須，先主嘲之曰：「昔吾居涿縣，特多毛姓，東西南北皆諸毛也，涿令稱曰『諸毛繞涿居乎』！

translations.literal: At first, when the First Sovereign met Liu Zhang at Fu, at the time Yu was Zhang's aide, attending the seat; the man was abundant in beard; the First Sovereign mocked him saying, "Formerly I dwelt in Zhuo county—especially many Mao surnames; east, west, south, north were all the various Mao; the Zhuo magistrate said 'All the Mao surround Zhuo dwelling!'"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei once met Liu Zhang at Fu, Zhang Yu was present with his heavy beard. Liu Bei teased him that in Zhuo county every direction had been full of people surnamed Mao—“all the Maos around Zhuo,” the magistrate had joked.

sentences.zh: 」裕即答曰：「昔有作上黨潞長，遷為涿令者，去官還家，時人與書，欲署潞則失涿，欲署涿則失潞，乃署曰：『潞涿君』。

translations.literal: " Yu immediately replied saying, "Formerly there was one who was Lu district chief of Shangdang, promoted to Zhuo magistrate; leaving office returning home, when people wrote letters, wishing to sign Lu then lost Zhuo, wishing to sign Zhuo then lost Lu—thereupon signed saying 'Lord Lu-Zhuo.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu shot back with the tale of a Lu district chief of Shangdang promoted to Zhuo magistrate whom correspondents could only address as “Lord Lu-Zhuo,” lest either place name be dropped.

sentences.zh: 先主無須，故裕以此及之。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign had no beard; therefore Yu with this reached him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was beardless, so Zhang Yu turned the jest on him.

sentences.zh: 先主常銜莫不遜，加忿其漏言，乃顯裕諫爭漢中不驗，下獄，將誅之。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign constantly bore resentment at his lack of deference, added anger at his leaking words, then displayed Yu's remonstrance contending Hanzhong not verified, cast into prison, about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei long resented his rudeness and, furious that he had spread prophecies, seized on his mistaken counsel about Hanzhong, threw him in prison, and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮表請其罪，先主答曰：「勞蘭生門，不得不鋤。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang memorialized requesting his crime; the First Sovereign answered saying, "Orchid grows at the door—one cannot but hoe it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang pleaded for him, but Liu Bei answered, “Weeds at the gate must be cut.”

sentences.zh: 」裕遂棄市。

translations.literal: " Yu thereupon was exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu was then executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 後魏氏之立，先主之薨，皆如裕所刻。

translations.literal: Later Wei's establishment, the First Sovereign's passing—all as Yu had inscribed.
translations.idiomatic: The founding of Wei and Liu Bei’s death fell out as Zhang Yu had predicted.

sentences.zh: 又曉相術，每舉鏡視面，自知刑死，未常不撲之於地也。

translations.literal: Again he understood physiognomy; each time raising mirror viewing face, himself knew execution death, always dashed it to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He also knew physiognomy; whenever he looked in a mirror and saw he was fated for execution, he flung it down.

sentences.zh: 羣卒，子臣頗傳其術。

translations.literal: When Qun died, his son Chen somewhat transmitted his art.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Qun died, his son Zhou Chen inherited something of his art.

sentences.zh: 杜瓊字伯瑜，蜀郡成都人也。

translations.literal: Du Qiong, courtesy name Boyu, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qiong, styled Boyu, was a native of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少受學於任安，精究安術。

translations.literal: In youth he received learning from Ren An, penetratingly investigated An's arts.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Ren An and mastered his techniques.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時辟為從事，先主定益州，領牧，以瓊為議曹從事。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time summoned as staff aide; the First Sovereign settled Yizhou, led governorship, appointed Qiong deliberation-cohort aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he was a staff aide; after Liu Bei took Yizhou he made him an aide in the deliberation cohort.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，拜諫議大夫，遷左中郎將、大鴻臚、太常。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, appointed grandee remonstrant, promoted general of the household of the left, grand herald, grand master of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shan took the throne Du Qiong became grandee remonstrant, then general of the household of the left, grand herald, and grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 為人靜默少言，闔門自守，不與世事。

translations.literal: As a man he was quiet and still, few words, closed gate self-guarding, did not join worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was quiet and reticent, kept to his house, and shunned public affairs.

sentences.zh: 蔣琬、費禕等皆器重之。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and others all deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and others held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 雖學業入深，初不視天文有所論說。

translations.literal: Although learning entered deep, at first did not view astronomy to have discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Though deeply learned in the classics, he refused to discourse on astrology.

sentences.zh: 後近通儒譙周常問其意，瓊答曰：「欲明此術甚難，須當身視，識其形色，不可信人也。

translations.literal: Later the nearby thorough scholar Qiao Zhou often asked his meaning; Qiong answered saying, "To clarify this art is very hard; one must personally view, recognize its form and color—one cannot trust others."
translations.idiomatic: When Qiao Zhou pressed him, Du Qiong said the art was hard to master without seeing the omens oneself and could not be taken on hearsay.

sentences.zh: 晨夜苦劇，然後知之，復憂漏洩，不如不知，是以不復視也。

translations.literal: Dawn and night bitter toil, then afterward knowing it; again fearing leakage—better not to know—therefore no longer viewing.
translations.idiomatic: It meant toil day and night, and even then one risked leaking secrets—better not to know—so he ceased observing the sky.

sentences.zh: 」周因問曰：「昔周徵君以為當塗高者魏也，其義何也？

translations.literal: " Zhou thereupon asked saying, "Formerly Zhou the summonee thought dangtu gao was Wei—what was its meaning?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou then asked what Zhou Shu had meant by saying “dangtu gao” was Wei.

sentences.zh: 」瓊答曰：「魏，闕名也，當塗而高，聖人取類而言耳。

translations.literal: " Qiong answered saying, "Wei is the name of the palace gate tower; standing on the road and high—the sage took category to speak."
translations.idiomatic: Du Qiong replied that wei was the name of the palace gate—“blocking the road and high”—and the sage had spoken by analogy.

sentences.zh: 」又問周曰：「寧復有所怪邪？

translations.literal: " Again asked Zhou saying, "Is there yet something strange?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Qiao Zhou whether anything else seemed odd.

sentences.zh: 」周曰：「未達也。

translations.literal: " Zhou said, "I have not understood."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou said he did not understand.

sentences.zh: 」瓊又曰：「古者名官職不言曹，始自漢已來，名官盡言曹。

translations.literal: " Qiong again said, "In antiquity naming offices did not say cao; beginning from Han onward, naming offices all say cao."
translations.idiomatic: Du Qiong added that ancient offices were not called cao, but since Han every bureau had been called cao.

sentences.zh: 吏言屬曹，卒言侍曹，此殆天意也。」

translations.literal: Clerks speak belonging cao; soldiers speak attending cao—this is nearly heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks belonged to cao, guards attended cao—perhaps this was Heaven’s hint.

sentences.zh: 瓊年八十餘，延熙十三年卒。

translations.literal: Qiong past eighty sui, in the thirteenth year of Yanxi died.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qiong died in 250, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 著《韓詩章句》十餘萬言，不教諸子，內學無傳業者。

translations.literal: He authored Han shi zhangju over a hundred thousand words; did not teach his sons; inner learning had none who transmitted the occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than a hundred thousand characters on the Han shi but taught none of his sons his occult learning, so it died with him.

sentences.zh: 周緣瓊言，乃觸類而長之曰：

translations.literal: Zhou following Qiong's words, then touching categories and extending them said:
translations.idiomatic: Building on Du Qiong’s hints, Qiao Zhou elaborated:

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》著秦穆候名太子曰仇，弟曰成師。

translations.literal: The Zuo commentary records Duke Mu of Qin named the heir apparent Chou, the younger brother Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition records how Duke Mu of Qin named his heir Chou and his younger son Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 師服曰：『異哉君之名子也！

translations.literal: Shi Fu said: 'Strange indeed, lord, in naming your sons!'
translations.idiomatic: Shi Fu cried, “Strange indeed, my lord, how you have named your sons!”

sentences.zh: 嘉耦曰妃，怨耦曰仇，今君名太子曰仇，弟曰成師，始兆亂矣，兄其替乎？

translations.literal: A blessed pair is called fei; a resentful pair is called chou; now the lord names the heir apparent Chou, the younger Chengsi—this begins the omen of chaos; will the elder be replaced?'
translations.idiomatic: A good match is fei and a bad match chou; to name the elder Chou and the younger “completed armies” was an omen of strife—would the elder not be cast down?'

sentences.zh: 』其後果如服言。

translations.literal: ' Afterward it indeed was as Fu said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved Shi Fu right.

sentences.zh: 及漢靈帝名二子曰史候、董候，既立為帝，後皆免為諸侯，與師服言相似也。

translations.literal: When Han Lingdi named two sons Marquis of Shi and Marquis of Dong, once established as emperors, afterward both were demoted to feudal lords—similar to Shi Fu's words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling’s sons, the Marquises of Shi and Dong, were enthroned and then degraded like Shi Fu’s warning.

sentences.zh: 先主諱備，其訓具也，後主諱禪，其訓授也，如言劉已具矣，當授與人也；

translations.literal: The First Sovereign's taboo Bei, its gloss is 'complete'; the Later Sovereign's taboo Shan, its gloss is 'hand over'—as if saying Liu is already complete, ought to hand over to others;
translations.idiomatic: The Former Ruler’s name Bei means “complete,” and the Later Ruler’s name Shan means “to hand over”—as if to say the house of Liu was complete and must be yielded to another;

sentences.zh: 意者甚於穆候、靈帝之名子。

translations.literal: the meaning is graver than Duke Mu's or Lingdi's naming sons.
translations.idiomatic: a darker omen than Duke Mu’s or Emperor Ling’s choice of names.

sentences.zh: 後宦人黃皓弄權於內，景耀五年，宮中大樹無故自折，周深憂之，無所與言，乃書柱曰：「眾而大，期之會，具而授，若何復？

translations.literal: Later the eunuch Huang Hao toyed with power within; in the fifth year of Jingyao, a great tree in the palace for no reason broke itself; Zhou deeply worried, having none to speak with, then wrote on a pillar saying: "Many and great, the appointed meeting; complete and hand over—how again?"
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Huang Hao dominated the court, a great tree in the palace snapped in 262 without wind. Qiao Zhou brooded in silence and wrote on a pillar: “Many and great, the hour of meeting; complete and handed over—what renewal?”

sentences.zh: 」言曹者眾也，魏者大也，眾而大，天下其當會也，具而授，如何復有立者乎？

translations.literal: " Explaining: cao means multitude; wei means great; many and great—the realm ought to unite; complete and hand over—how could there again be one who stands?
translations.idiomatic: Cao means “crowd,” Wei means “great”—a great host gathers and the realm is united; once all is handed over, who could still stand?

sentences.zh: 蜀既亡，咸以周言為驗。

translations.literal: When Shu was already lost, all took Zhou's words as verified.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, everyone said Qiao Zhou had been proved right.

sentences.zh: 周曰：「此雖己所推尋，然有所因，由杜君之辭而廣之耳，殊無神思獨至之異也。」

translations.literal: Zhou said, "This although myself I pushed and sought, yet had what it followed from—by Lord Du's words I broadened it; utterly no spirit-thought uniquely arriving's strangeness."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou said he had only reasoned it out from Du Qiong’s words and claimed no supernatural insight of his own.

sentences.zh: 許慈字仁篤，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ci, courtesy name Rendu, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ci, styled Rendu, was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 師事劉熙，善鄭氏學，治《易》、《尚書》、《三禮》、《毛詩》、《論語》。

translations.literal: He studied under Liu Xi, was good at Zheng's learning, worked on the Changes, Documents, three Rites, Mao Odes, Analects.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Xi, mastered the Zheng school, and lectured on the Changes, Documents, three Rites, Mao Odes, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 建安中，與許靖等俱自交州入蜀。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an period, together with Xu Jing and others all from Jiaozhou entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jian’an years he came to Shu from Jiaozhou with Xu Jing and others.

sentences.zh: 時又有魏郡胡潛，字公興，不知其所以在益土。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Hu Qian of Wei commandery, courtesy name Gongxing; not known why he was in Yi soil.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Hu Qian of Wei commandery, styled Gongxing, of uncertain origin in Shu.

sentences.zh: 潛雖學不沾洽，然卓犖強識，祖宗制度之儀，喪紀五服之數，皆指掌畫地，舉手可採。

translations.literal: Although Qian's learning was not comprehensive, yet outstanding and strong in memory, rites of ancestor institutions, mourning gradations and five garments' numbers—all as pointing palm drawing on ground, raising hand could gather.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qian was not broadly read but had a formidable memory: ancestral ritual and the degrees of mourning he could trace on the ground from his fingertips.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，承喪亂歷紀，學業衰廢，乃鳩合典籍，沙汰眾學。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu, inheriting mourning and chaos through eras, learning occupation decayed and abandoned, thereupon gathered canons and records, sifted and washed the host of learning.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars Liu Bei gathered the classics, culled scholars, and tried to revive learning.

sentences.zh: 慈、潛並為學士，與孟光、來敏等典掌舊文。

translations.literal: Ci and Qian together became academicians, with Meng Guang, Lai Min, and others canonically grasping old texts.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ci and Hu Qian became academicians with Meng Guang and Lai Min in charge of the old texts.

sentences.zh: 值庶事草創，動多疑議，慈、潛更相剋伐，謗讟忿急，形於聲色；

translations.literal: Meeting the hundred affairs grass beginning, movements much doubtful debate; Ci and Qian alternately attacked each other, slander and malice angry and hasty, shown in voice and countenance;
translations.idiomatic: While institutions were still being founded they disputed every point, Xu Ci and Hu Qian sniped at each other with open bitterness;

sentences.zh: 書籍有無，不相通借，時尋楚撻，以相震攇。

translations.literal: Books' having or not, did not mutually lend; at times sought Chu flogging, thereby mutually to threaten.
translations.idiomatic: they would not lend each other books and even threatened one another with blows.

sentences.zh: 〈攇，虛晚反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Xian is read xu-wan fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The commentary gives a fanqie spelling for this graph, reading xu-wan.〉

sentences.zh: 其矜己妒彼，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Their priding self and envying the other reached even to this.
translations.idiomatic: Their vanity and mutual jealousy went that far.

sentences.zh: 先主愍其若斯，羣僚大會，使倡家假為二子之容，效其訟鬩之狀，酒酣樂作，以為嬉戲。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign pitied them being thus; the host of officials great assembly; he caused entertainers to feign the two sons' forms, imitate their lawsuit-quarrel's appearance; when wine was deep music rose, taking it as jest and play.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei pitied them and, at a banquet of the full court, had actors mimic the two scholars and act out their quarrel for sport when the wine flowed and music struck up.

sentences.zh: 初以辭義相難，終以刀杖相屈，用感切之。

translations.literal: At first with words and meaning they mutually challenged; in the end with knives and staves mutually submitted—thereby to move and cut them.
translations.idiomatic: The skit began with verbal sparring and ended with mock blows, meant to shame them into reform.

sentences.zh: 潛先沒，慈後主世稍遷至大長秋，卒。

translations.literal: Qian died first; Ci in the Later Sovereign's age gradually was promoted to grand prolonger of autumn, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qian died first; under the Later Ruler Xu Ci rose step by step to grand prolonger of autumn and then died.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：蜀少人士，故慈、潛等並見載述。〉

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng states: Shu had few men of letters; therefore Ci, Qian, and others were together recorded in narrative.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng remarks that Shu had few scholars, so figures like Xu Ci and Hu Qian earned a place in the record.〉

sentences.zh: 子勳傳其業，復為博士。

translations.literal: The son Xun transmitted his occupation; again became erudite.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu Xun inherited his learning and also became a court erudite.

sentences.zh: 孟光字孝裕，河南洛陽人，漢太尉孟鬱之族。

translations.literal: Meng Guang, courtesy name Xiaoyu, a man of Luoyang in Henan, of the clan of Han Grand Commandant Meng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guang, styled Xiaoyu, was a native of Luoyang in Henan and a kinsman of Han grand commandant Meng Yu.

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢書》曰：鬱，中常侍孟賁之弟。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Xu Han shu states: Yu was younger brother of palace attendant Meng Ben.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Han shu identifies Meng Yu as the younger brother of the eunuch Meng Ben.〉

sentences.zh: 靈帝末為講部吏。

translations.literal: At the end of Lingdi's reign he was lecturer-section clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Ling’s reign he served as a clerk in the lecture office.

sentences.zh: 獻帝遷都長安，遂逃人蜀，劉焉父子待以客禮。

translations.literal: When Xiandi moved the capital to Chang'an, thereupon he fled and entered Shu; Liu Yan and son treated him with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to Chang'an, he fled into Shu, where Liu Yan and Liu Zhang received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 博物識古，無書不覽，尤銳意三史，長於漢家舊典。

translations.literal: Broad in things and knowing antiquity, no book he did not peruse; especially keen intent on the three histories, excelled in Han house old canons.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read in antiquity, pored especially over the three histories, and knew the Han statutes better than most.

sentences.zh: 好《公羊春秋》而譏呵《左氏》，每與來敏爭此二義，光常譊譊讙咋。

translations.literal: He loved Gongyang Spring and Autumn and sneered at Zuo's; each time with Lai Min he disputed these two meanings; Guang constantly bickered clamored and snapped.
translations.idiomatic: He favored the Gongyang tradition and mocked the Zuo commentary, and whenever he debated the two with Lai Min he grew loud and quarrelsome.

sentences.zh: 〈譊音奴交反。

translations.literal: 〈Nao is read nu-jiao fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character nao is read with the fanqie nu-jiao.

sentences.zh: 讙音休袁反。

translations.literal: Huan is read xiu-yuan fan.
translations.idiomatic: The character huan is read with the fanqie xiu-yuan.

sentences.zh: 咋音徂格反。〉

translations.literal: Za is read zu-ge fan.〉
translations.idiomatic: The character za is read with the fanqie zu-ge.〉

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，拜為儀郎，與許慈等並掌制度。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled Yizhou, appointed him gentleman of ceremony, with Xu Ci and others together grasping institutions.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took Yizhou he named him gentleman of ceremony and put him with Xu Ci and others in charge of ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，為符節令、屯騎校尉、長樂少府，遷大司農。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, he became Bearer of Credentials, Colonel of Garrisoned Cavalry, junior steward of Eternal Joy, promoted grand minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Shan he served as bearer of credentials, colonel of garrisoned cavalry, junior steward of the Eternal Joy palace, and then grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 延熙九年秋，大赦，光於眾中責大將軍費禕曰：「夫赦者，偏枯之物，非明世所宜有也。

translations.literal: In autumn of the ninth year of Yanxi, great amnesty; Guang in the crowd rebuked Grand General Fei Yi saying, "Now amnesty is a withered-on-one-side thing—not what an enlightened age ought to have."
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 246, when a general amnesty was proclaimed, Meng Guang publicly rebuked general-in-chief Fei Yi: amnesties are a crutch unfit for an enlightened reign.

sentences.zh: 衰弊窮極，必不得已，然後乃可權而行之耳。

translations.literal: Decline and exhaustion extreme, must be without choice, then afterward may by expediency carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: Only when decay is extreme and there is truly no alternative may one use them as a temporary measure."

sentences.zh: 今主上仁賢，百僚稱職，有何旦夕之危，倒懸之急，而數施非常之恩，以惠姦宄之惡乎？

translations.literal: Now the lord above is humane and worthy, hundred officials fit their posts—what dawn-and-dusk peril, upside-down hanging's urgency, that repeatedly you apply extraordinary grace to benefit villainy's evil?"
translations.idiomatic: Our ruler is humane and able, the bureaucracy competent—where is the crisis that justifies repeated extraordinary mercy to the benefit of criminals?"

sentences.zh: 又鷹隼始擊，而更原宥有罪，上犯天時，下違人理。

translations.literal: Again hawks and falcons first strike, yet you further pardon those with guilt—above offends heaven's season, below violates human principle."
translations.idiomatic: This is the season when the law should strike like hawks; to pardon offenders now offends both Heaven and human sense."

sentences.zh: 老夫耄朽，不達治體，窮謂其法難以經久，豈具瞻之高美，所望於明德哉。

translations.literal: This old man decrepit and rotten, does not comprehend governance's body; utterly deem this law hard to endure long—how is the high beauty all look up to what the enlightened virtue expects?"
translations.idiomatic: I am old and dull, yet even I see that such policy cannot last—is this what we expect of a leader the world admires?"

sentences.zh: 」禕但顧謝踧踖而已。

translations.literal: " Yi only looked and apologized, cramped and uneasy, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi could only apologize awkwardly.

sentences.zh: 光之指摘痛癢，多如是類。

translations.literal: Guang's pointing and plucking of pain and itch was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guang’s blunt criticisms were often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 故執政重臣，心不能悅，爵位不登，每直言無所迴避，為代所嫌。

translations.literal: Therefore those who held government as weighty ministers, hearts could not be pleased; noble rank did not ascend; each time straight words without evasion—by the age was resented.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ministers could not abide him, his rank rose no higher, and his blunt speech made him disliked at court.

sentences.zh: 太常廣漢鐔承、

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Tan Cheng of Guanghan,
translations.idiomatic: Tan Cheng of Guanghan, grand master of ceremonies,

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：承字公文，歷郡守少府。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Huayang guo zhi states: Cheng's courtesy name Gongwen; passed through commandery governor and junior privy treasurer.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang guo zhi gives his style as Gongwen and notes he served as governor and junior privy treasurer.〉

sentences.zh: 光祿勛河東裴儁等，年資皆在光後，而登據上列，處光之右，蓋以此也。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Household Pei Jun of Hedong and others, years and seniority all were behind Guang, yet ascended and occupied upper ranks, placed to Guang's right—probably because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun of Hedong and others, though junior to Meng Guang, stood above him in rank—likely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 〈傅暢《裴氏家記》曰：儁字奉先，魏尚書令潛弟也。

translations.literal: 〈Fu Chang's Pei shi jiaji states: Jun's courtesy name Fengxian, younger brother of Wei Masters of Writing Ling Pei Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang’s Pei family record names him Fengxian, younger brother of Wei director of the secretariat Pei Qian.

sentences.zh: 儁姊夫爲蜀中長史，儁送之，時年十餘歲，遂遭漢末大亂，不復得還。

translations.literal: Jun's elder sister's husband was chief clerk in Shu; Jun saw him off; at the time age over ten sui; thereupon encountered Han end great chaos, no more able to return.
translations.idiomatic: He had escorted a brother-in-law serving as chief clerk in Shu while still a boy and was stranded by the late-Han turmoil.

sentences.zh: 既長知名，爲蜀所推重也。

translations.literal: Having grown, became known, was by Shu pushed and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Grown famous, he was highly regarded in Shu.

sentences.zh: 子越，字令緒，爲蜀督軍。

translations.literal: Son Yue, courtesy name Lingxu, was Shu army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pei Yue, styled Lingxu, became an army supervisor in Shu.

sentences.zh: 蜀破，遷還洛陽，拜議郎。〉

translations.literal: Shu broken, moved back to Luoyang, appointed gentleman consultant.〉
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he returned to Luoyang as gentleman consultant.〉

sentences.zh: 後進文士秘書郎郤正數從光諮訪，光問正太子所習讀性並其性情好尚，正答曰：「奉親虔恭。

translations.literal: Later-advanced literary gentleman secretary Xi Zheng several times followed Guang to consult; Guang asked Zheng what the heir apparent studied, read, nature together his disposition likes and dislikes; Zheng answered saying, "Serving kin reverent and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary Xi Zheng often consulted Meng Guang, who asked about the crown prince’s studies and tastes. Xi Zheng replied that he served his parents with reverence.

sentences.zh: 夙夜匪懈，有古世子之風；

translations.literal: Dawn and night not slack—has ancient heir's wind;
translations.idiomatic: He toils day and night without slack, in the manner of a classical heir;

sentences.zh: 接待羣僚，舉動出於仁恕。

translations.literal: Receiving the host of officials, movements issue from benevolence and forbearance."
translations.idiomatic: and toward his staff he acts with benevolence and forbearance."

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「如君所道，皆家戶所有耳；

translations.literal: " Guang said, "As you, sir, relate—these are all what every household has;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guang said, “What you describe any decent household could claim;

sentences.zh: 吾今所問，欲知其權略智調何如也。

translations.literal: what I now ask is to wish to know his stratagem and wit, wisdom and adjustment—how are they?"
translations.idiomatic: I want to know his resourcefulness and wit."

sentences.zh: 」正曰：「世子之道，在於承志竭歡，既不得妄有所施為，且智調藏於胸懷，權略應時而發，此之有無，焉可豫設也？

translations.literal: " Zheng said, "The heir's way lies in inheriting intent and exhausting joy; since he cannot rashly have something to enact, moreover wisdom and adjustment hide in breast and bosom, stratagem and wit respond to season and issue—this having or not, how can it be prearranged?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng answered that an heir’s duty is to please his father; he cannot act on his own, and whether he has deep judgment shows only when the moment comes—it cannot be rehearsed in advance."

sentences.zh: 」光解正慎宜，不為放談，乃曰：「吾好直言，無所迴避，每彈射利病，為世人所譏嫌。

translations.literal: " Guang understood Zheng was cautious and proper, did not indulge loose talk, then said, "I love straight speech, nothing evaded; each time I shoot maladies—by the age am mocked and resented.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Xi Zheng’s reserve, Meng Guang said he loved blunt speech that exposed faults and was therefore mocked by the world.

sentences.zh: 疑省君意亦不甚好吾言，然語有次。

translations.literal: I suspect examining your mind also does not much love my words, yet speech has order.
translations.idiomatic: You may not care for my words, yet there is a point to their order.

sentences.zh: 今天下未定，智意為先，智意雖有自然，然不可力強致也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is not settled; wisdom and intent come first; wisdom and intent although there is what is natural, yet cannot by force be compelled to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is unsettled: judgment matters first. Some have it by nature, but it cannot be forced.

sentences.zh: 此儲君讀書，寧當效吾等竭力博識以待訪問，如博士探策講試以求爵位邪！

translations.literal: This stored lord's reading—ought he imitate us exhausting strength broad knowledge to await inquiry, like erudites drawing slips lecturing examination to seek noble rank!
translations.idiomatic: Should the heir cram like an erudite grinding for examination and rank?

sentences.zh: 當務其急者。

translations.literal: Ought to attend to what is urgent."
translations.idiomatic: He should master what is urgent."

sentences.zh: 」正深謂光言為然。

translations.literal: " Zheng deeply deemed Guang's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 後光坐事免官，年九十餘，卒。

translations.literal: Later Guang because of affair was dismissed from office; past ninety sui, died.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guang was later stripped of office for an offense and died in his nineties.

sentences.zh: 來敏字敬達，義陽新野人，來歙之後也。

translations.literal: Lai Min, courtesy name Jingda, a man of Xinye in Yiyang, was posterity of Lai Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Min, styled Jingda, from Xinye in Yiyang, was a descendant of Lai Xi.

sentences.zh: 父艷，為漢司空。

translations.literal: Father Yan was Han Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lai Yan had been Han minister of works.

sentences.zh: 〈華嶠《後漢書》曰：艷好學下士，開館養徒眾。

translations.literal: 〈Hua Qiao's Hou Han shu states: Yan loved learning and lowered himself to gentlemen, opened a hall and raised disciples many.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao’s Later Han history says Lai Yan loved learning, honored scholars, and kept a school with many pupils.

sentences.zh: 少歷顯位，靈帝時位至司空。〉

translations.literal: In youth passed through eminent posts; in Lingdi's time rank reached Minister of Works.〉
translations.idiomatic: He rose young to high office and under Emperor Ling became minister of works.〉

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，敏隨姊夫奔荊州，姊夫黃琬是劉璋祖母之侄，故璋遣迎琬妻，敏遂俱與姊入蜀，常為璋賓客。

translations.literal: Han end great chaos; Min followed elder sister's husband fleeing to Jing Province; elder sister's husband Huang Wan was Liu Zhang's grandmother's nephew; therefore Zhang sent to welcome Wan's wife; Min thereupon together with elder sister entered Shu, constantly was Zhang's guest.
translations.idiomatic: In the late-Han turmoil Lai Min fled to Jingzhou with his brother-in-law Huang Wan, a nephew of Liu Zhang’s grandmother. When Liu Zhang sent for Huang Wan’s wife, Lai Min accompanied his sister into Shu and stayed on as Liu Zhang’s client.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書籍，善《左氏春秋》，尤精於《倉》、《雅》訓詁，好是正文字。

translations.literal: Broadly perused books and records, good at Zuo's Spring and Autumn, especially refined in Cangjie and Erya glosses, loved to correct graphs.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, excelled at the Zuo tradition, was expert in the Cangjie and Erya glossaries, and loved to emend characters.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，署敏典學校尉。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled Yizhou, appointed Min colonel director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei made him colonel director of studies after taking Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及立太子，以為家令。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was established, made him household commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was installed he became household commandant.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，為虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, became gentleman of the household for rapid as tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Shan he became a gentleman of the household of the rapid tigers.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮住漢中，請為軍祭酒、輔軍將軍，坐事去職。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang lodged at Hanzhong, requested him as army libationer, general who assists the army; because of affair removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang at Hanzhong named him army libationer and general who assists the army, then removed him for an offense.

sentences.zh: 〈亮集有教曰：「將軍來敏對上官顯言『新人有何功德而奪我榮資與之邪？

translations.literal: 〈In Liang's collected works there is an instruction saying: "General Lai Min to superiors openly said 'What merit have newcomers that they seize my glory and stipend and give to them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang’s papers record Lai Min complaining aloud to his superiors: “What merit have these newcomers that they take my honors and pay?”

sentences.zh: 諸人共憎我，何故如是』？

translations.literal: The host together hate me—why reason thus?'"
translations.idiomatic: “Everyone despises me—why is it so?”"

sentences.zh: 敏年老狂悖，生此怨言。

translations.literal: Min old age mad perverse, produced these resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: In old age Lai Min grew wild and uttered these resentments.

sentences.zh: 昔成都初定，議者以為來敏亂羣，先帝以新定之際，故遂含容，無所禮用。

translations.literal: Formerly when Chengdu was first settled, debaters thought Lai Min disturbed the host; the First Sovereign because newly settled occasion, therefore then contained him, without employing him in ritual posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu was first taken, many said Lai Min unsettled the court; the late emperor tolerated him while order was new and gave him no real post.

sentences.zh: 後劉子初選以為太子家令，先帝不悅而不忍拒也。

translations.literal: Later Liu Zichu selected him as heir's household commandant; the First Sovereign was not pleased yet could not bear to refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Ba chose him as household commandant to the heir; the late emperor disliked the choice but would not overrule it.

sentences.zh: 後主既位，吾闇於知人，遂復擢為將軍祭酒，違議者之審見，背先帝所疏外，自謂能以敦厲薄俗，帥之以義。

translations.literal: After the Later Sovereign had the throne, I was dark in knowing men, thereupon again raised him as general's libationer, contrary to debaters' careful view, turning back what the First Sovereign had kept at distance, self-deemed able with sternness to urge thin customs, lead them with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: After I took power I misjudged men and promoted him again as libationer to the general, against good counsel and the late emperor’s distrust, thinking I could reform custom by example.

sentences.zh: 今既不能，表退職，使閉門思愆。」〉

translations.literal: Now already cannot; memorialize dismissal from office, cause closed gate to ponder faults."〉
translations.idiomatic: That failed; I now memorialize his removal and confinement at home for reflection."〉

sentences.zh: 亮卒後，還成都為大長秋，又免，後累遷為光祿大夫，復坐過黜。

translations.literal: After Liang died, returned to Chengdu as grand prolonger of autumn, again dismissed; later accumulated promotions to grandee grand of the household, again because of fault demoted.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang’s death he returned to Chengdu as grand prolonger of autumn, was dismissed again, rose to grandee grand of the household, and was demoted once more for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 前後數貶削，皆以語言不節，舉動違常也。

translations.literal: Before and after several demotions and cuts, all because speech lacked restraint, movements violated the norm.
translations.idiomatic: His repeated demotions all stemmed from intemperate speech and irregular conduct.

sentences.zh: 時孟光亦以樞機不慎，議論干時，然猶愈於敏，俱以耆宿學士見禮於世。

translations.literal: At the time Meng Guang also because pivot and bolt was not careful, discussion touched the times, yet still better than Min; both by old-host erudite were shown ritual in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guang too was careless in speech and meddled in policy, yet he was still steadier than Lai Min; both were honored as venerable scholars.

sentences.zh: 而敏荊楚名族，東宮舊臣，特加優待，是故廢而復起。

translations.literal: But Min was Jing-Chu famous clan, eastern palace old minister—specially added favor and treatment; therefore dismissed yet again raised.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Min came from a great Jing-Chu clan and had served the heir early, so he received special favor and was restored after dismissal.

sentences.zh: 後以敏為執慎將軍，欲令以官重自警戒也，年九十七，景耀中卒。

translations.literal: Later made Min General Who Holds Caution, wishing to cause him by office weight to self warn and guard; at ninety-seven sui, died in the Jingyao period.
translations.idiomatic: He was later named general who holds caution so the dignity of office might restrain him; he died in the Jingyao years at ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 子忠，亦博覽經學，有敏風，與尚書向充等並能協贊大將軍姜維。

translations.literal: Son Zhong, also broadly viewed classics learning, had Min's manner; with Masters of Writing Xiang Chong and others together could assist and aid Grand General Jiang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lai Zhong was widely read like his father and, with Xiang Chong of the secretariat and others, ably supported general-in-chief Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 維善之，以為參軍。

translations.literal: Wei deemed him good, made him aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei valued him and made him an aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 尹默字思潛，梓潼涪人也。

translations.literal: Yin Mo, courtesy name Siqian, was a man of Fu in Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Mo, styled Siqian, came from Fu in Zitong.

sentences.zh: 益部多貴今文而不祟章句，默知其不博。

translations.literal: Yi region mostly prized modern script and did not honor chapter-and-verse; Mo knew it was not broad.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou prized modern-text learning over philology; Yin Mo saw that as narrow.

sentences.zh: 乃遠遊荊州，從司馬德操、宋仲子等受古學。

translations.literal: Thereupon traveled far to Jing Province, followed Sima Decao, Song Zhongzi, and others to receive ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: He journeyed to Jingzhou to study antiquity under Sima Hui, Song Zhongzi, and others.

sentences.zh: 皆通諸經史，又專精於《左氏春秋》，自劉歆條例，鄭眾、賈逵父子、陳元、方服虔注說，咸略誦述，不復按本。

translations.literal: All penetrated the various classics and histories; again specialized in Zuo's Spring and Autumn—from Liu Xin's regulations, Zheng Zhong, Jia Kui father and son, Chen Yuan, down to Fu Qian's commentary explanations, all broadly recited and narrated, no longer checking the original.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and histories and specialized in the Zuo commentary, reciting from memory Liu Xin's outline and the glosses of Zheng Zhong, the Jias, Chen Yuan, and Fu Qian without opening the text.

sentences.zh: 先主定益州，領牧，以為勸學從事。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled Yizhou, led governorship, appointed him encourage-learning aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei became governor of Yizhou he named Yin Mo encourage-learning aide.

sentences.zh: 及立太子，以默為僕，射以《左氏傳》授後主。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was established, appointed Mo as steward, archer used Zuo's Commentary to instruct the Later Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was installed, Yin Mo was made his junior tutor and taught him the Zuo commentary.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, appointed grandee remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shan took the throne Yin Mo became grandee remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮住漢中，請為軍祭酒。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang lodged at Hanzhong, requested him as army libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang at Hanzhong appointed him army libationer.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，還成都，拜大中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Liang died; returned to Chengdu, appointed grandee grand, died.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang died he returned to Chengdu as grandee grand and died there.

sentences.zh: 子宗傳其業，為博士。

translations.literal: Son Zong transmitted his occupation; became erudite.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin Zong inherited his scholarship and became an erudite.

sentences.zh: 〈宋仲子後在魏。

translations.literal: 〈Song Zhongzi afterward was in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhongzi later lived in Wei.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：其子與魏諷謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: The Wei lue states: His son with Wei Feng plotted rebellion, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue says his son joined Wei Feng’s plot and was executed.

sentences.zh: 魏太子答王朗書曰：「昔石厚與州吁遊，父碏知其與亂；

translations.literal: Wei crown prince answered Wang Lang's letter saying: "Formerly Shi Hou roamed with Zhou Xu; father Que knew he would join chaos;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei crown prince wrote Wang Lang that when Shi Hou kept company with Zhou Xu, his father Shi Que foresaw rebellion;

sentences.zh: 韓子暱田蘇，穆子知其好仁：故君子遊必有方，居必就士，誠有以也。

translations.literal: Hanzi was intimate with Tian Su; Muzi knew he loved benevolence—therefore the gentleman's roaming must have direction, dwelling must approach gentlemen—truly there is reason."
translations.idiomatic: and when Han Qi drew close to Tian Su, Muzhi saw his humane bent—so a gentleman chooses his company and neighbors with care."

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 宋忠無石子先識之明，老罹此禍。

translations.literal: Song Zhong lacked Shi Zixian's foresight; old suffered this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhong lacked the foresight of Shi Zixian and in old age met this disaster.

sentences.zh: 今雖欲原行滅親之誅，立純臣之節，尚可得邪！」〉

translations.literal: Now although wishing to pardon conduct of destroying kin's punishment, establish pure minister's integrity—can it still be obtained!"〉
translations.idiomatic: Even if one wished to spare him and uphold the duty of a pure minister, could it be done?"〉

sentences.zh: 譙周字允南，巴西西充國人也。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou, courtesy name Yunnan, was a man of Xichongguo in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou, styled Yunnan, came from Xichongguo in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 父

translations.literal: Father
translations.idiomatic: His father

sentences.zh: （山幷）

translations.literal: (Shan with bing)
translations.idiomatic: (the graphs shan and bing)

sentences.zh: ，字榮始，治《尚書》，兼通諸經及圖緯。

translations.literal: , courtesy name Rongshi, worked on the Documents, concurrently penetrated the various classics and charts and weft-texts.
translations.idiomatic: , styled Rongshi, studied the Documents and was versed in the classics and prognosticatory texts.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟請，皆不應，州就假師友從事。

translations.literal: Province and commandery summoned and invited—all did not respond; province then provisionally made mentor-and-friend aide.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every provincial and commandery summons, so the province named him mentor-and-friend on staff in name only.

sentences.zh: 周幼孤，與母兄同居。

translations.literal: Zhou in youth was orphaned, dwelt together with mother and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou was orphaned young and lived with his mother and elder brother.

sentences.zh: 既長，耽古篤學，家貧未嘗問產業，誦讀典籍，欣然獨笑，以忘寢食。

translations.literal: Having grown, addicted to antiquity and devoted to learning, family poor never inquired of estates; chanting and reading canons and records, gladly alone laughed, thereby forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he lost himself in ancient learning, ignored his poverty, and would chuckle over his books until he forgot meals and sleep.

sentences.zh: 研精《六經》，尤善書札，頗曉天文，而不以留意；

translations.literal: He ground fine the Six Classics, especially good at letters and notes, somewhat understood astronomy, yet did not with it pay attention;
translations.idiomatic: He plumbed the six classics, wrote fine letters, knew something of astronomy, but did not dwell on it;

sentences.zh: 諸子文章非心所存，不悉遍視也。

translations.literal: Various masters' writings were not what his heart stored; he did not all exhaustively view.
translations.idiomatic: he did not bother to read every philosopher’s essay.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，體貌素樸，性推誠不飾。

translations.literal: Body height eight chi, form and appearance plain and simple, nature pushing sincerity without adornment.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, looked plain and unadorned, and was sincere by nature.

sentences.zh: 無造次辯論之才，然潛識內敏。

translations.literal: Lacked hasty debate's talent, yet hidden knowledge inwardly keen.
translations.idiomatic: He was no quick debater but was inwardly acute.

sentences.zh: 建興中，丞相亮領益州牧，命周為勸學從事。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing period, Chancellor Liang led Governor of Yizhou, ordered Zhou as encourage-learning aide.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing, when Zhuge Liang governed Yizhou, he named Qiao Zhou encourage-learning aide.

sentences.zh: 〈《蜀記》曰：周初見亮，左右皆笑。

translations.literal: 〈The Shu ji states: When Zhou first saw Liang, those at left and right all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ji records that when Qiao Zhou first met Zhuge Liang, the attendants laughed.

sentences.zh: 既出，有司請推笑者，亮曰：「孤尚不能忍，況左右乎！」〉

translations.literal: After going out, the officials requested to pursue those who laughed; Liang said, "I alone still could not endure—how much more those at left and right!"〉
translations.idiomatic: When officials asked to punish the laughers, Zhuge Liang said he himself had barely kept a straight face—how could he blame the staff?〉

sentences.zh: 亮卒於敵庭，周在家聞問，即便奔赴，尋有詔書禁斷，惟周以速行得達。

translations.literal: Liang died in the enemy court; Zhou at home heard the news, thereupon at once hurried to go; soon there was an edict forbidding and cutting off—only Zhou by swift travel was able to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang died on campaign, Qiao Zhou rushed from home toward the funeral; an edict soon barred travel, but he moved fast enough to get through.

sentences.zh: 大將軍蔣琬領刺史，徙為典學從事，總州之學者。

translations.literal: Grand General Jiang Wan led inspector; Zhou was transferred to be aide in charge of studies, overseeing the province's scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Jiang Wan governed the province, Qiao Zhou was made aide overseeing studies and directed its scholars.

sentences.zh: 後主立太子，以周為僕，轉家令。

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign established the heir apparent, appointed Zhou as steward, transferred to household commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was named, Qiao Zhou became his steward and then household commandant.

sentences.zh: 時後主頗出遊觀，增廣聲樂。

translations.literal: At the time the Later Sovereign rather went out touring and viewing, increased and broadened sounds and music.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was often out touring and had expanded his music and entertainments.

sentences.zh: 周上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhou submitted a memorial remonstrating saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou submitted a memorial urging restraint:

sentences.zh: 昔王莽之敗，豪傑並起，跨州據郡，欲弄神器，於是賢才智士思望所歸，未必以其勢之廣狹，惟其德之薄厚也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Wang Mang failed, heroes rose together, straddling provinces and holding commanderies, wishing to toy with the sacred vessel; then worthy wise knights thought on whom to turn—not necessarily by their power's breadth or narrowness, only by their virtue's thinness or thickness.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell, warlords seized provinces and coveted the throne; wise men chose whom to follow by virtue, not by the size of a faction’s territory.

sentences.zh: 是故於時更始、公孫述及諸有大眾者多己廣大，然莫不快情恣欲，怠於為善，遊獵飲食，不恤民物。

translations.literal: Therefore at that time Gengshi, Gongsun Shu, and the various who had great hosts mostly deemed themselves vast and great, yet none did not indulge feelings and give free rein to desire, slack in doing good, roaming hunting eating and drinking, not pitying the people and things.
translations.idiomatic: Gengshi, Gongsun Shu, and others with large armies thought themselves mighty, yet all gave way to pleasure, neglected good rule, hunted and feasted, and ignored the people.

sentences.zh: 世祖初入河北，馮異等勸之曰：『當行人所不能為。

translations.literal: When the Shizu first entered Hebei, Feng Yi and others urged him saying, 'You ought to do what others cannot do.'
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwudi first entered Hebei, Feng Yi urged him to do what others could not.

sentences.zh: 』遂務理冤獄，節儉飲食，動尊法度，故北州歌歎，聲布四遠。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he strove to settle unjust prisons, was frugal in eating and drinking, movements honored law and measure; therefore the northern province sang praise, sound spread to the four distances.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared unjust cases, lived frugally, and honored the law, so the north praised him far and wide.

sentences.zh: 於是鄧禹自南陽追之，吳漢、寇恂未識世祖，遙聞德行，遂以權計舉漁陽、上谷突騎迎於廣阿。

translations.literal: Thereupon Deng Yu from Nanyang pursued him; Wu Han, Kou Xun had not yet known the Shizu, from afar heard virtue and conduct, thereupon by stratagem raised Yuyang and Shanggu shock cavalry to welcome him at Guang'a.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu followed from Nanyang; Wu Han and Kou Xun, though they had not met Guangwu, heard of his virtue and sent Yuyang and Shanggu cavalry to join him at Guang'a.

sentences.zh: 其望風慕德者邳肜、耿純、劉植之徒，至於輿病繼棺，繈負而至者，不可勝數，故能以弱為強，屠王郎，吞銅馬，折赤眉而成帝業也。

translations.literal: Those who gazed on the wind and admired virtue, Pi Tong, Geng Chun, Liu Zhi and their kind—even to carrying sickness and following coffins, swaddled on back and arriving—could not be counted; therefore was able with weak to become strong, slaughter Wang Lang, swallow Bronze Horse, break Red Eyebrows and complete emperor's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Tong, Geng Chun, Liu Zhi, and countless others sick or poor flocked to him, so he turned weakness into strength, destroyed Wang Lang and the Bronze Horse bands, broke the Red Eyebrows, and founded the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 及在洛陽，嘗欲小出，車駕已御，銚期諫曰：『天下未寧，臣誠不願陛下細行數出。

translations.literal: When at Luoyang, once wished a small outing; carriage team already harnessed; Yao Qi remonstrated saying, 'The realm is not yet tranquil; your servant truly does not wish Your Majesty small outings many times.'
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang, when Guangwu once meant a short outing with the chariot ready, Yao Qi urged him not to leave the capital often while the realm was still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 』即時還車。

translations.literal: ' At once returned the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned the chariot back at once.

sentences.zh: 及征隗囂，穎川盜起，世祖還洛陽，但遣寇恂往，恂曰：『穎川以陛下遠征，故奸猾起叛，未知陛下還，恐不時降；

translations.literal: When campaigning against Wei Ao, Yingchuan bandits rose; the Shizu returned to Luoyang, only sent Kou Xun to go; Xun said, 'Yingchuan because Your Majesty far campaigns, therefore the crafty rose in rebellion; not knowing Your Majesty has returned, I fear they will not soon submit;
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wei Ao, Yingchuan rebelled. Guangwu returned to Luoyang and would send only Kou Xun, who warned that the county would not yield until the emperor appeared in person.

sentences.zh: 陛下自臨，穎川賊必即降。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty personally attends, Yingchuan bandits certainly will at once submit.'
translations.idiomatic: If you go yourself, the rebels will surrender at once.'

sentences.zh: 』遂至穎川，竟如恂言。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon went to Yingchuan; in the end as Xun said.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Yingchuan and it fell as Kou Xun predicted.

sentences.zh: 故非急務，欲小出不敢，至於急務，欲自安不為，故帝者之欲善也如此！

translations.literal: Therefore for non-urgent affairs, wishing small outing did not dare; as for urgent affairs, wishing self ease did not do—therefore an emperor's desire for good was thus!
translations.idiomatic: Thus he would not stir for trifles but would not rest when duty called—such was an emperor’s zeal for good!

sentences.zh: 故《傳》曰『百姓不徒附』，誠以德先之也。

translations.literal: Therefore the tradition says 'The hundred surnames do not vainly attach'—truly because virtue leads them first.
translations.idiomatic: The classic says the people do not rally without cause—they follow virtue first.

sentences.zh: 今漢遭厄運，天下三分，雄哲之士思望之時也。

translations.literal: Now Han meets ill fortune; the realm is three parts; heroic wise knights are in a time of thinking whom to turn to.
translations.idiomatic: Han is in eclipse and the realm is split three ways—this is the hour when heroes look for a leader to trust.

sentences.zh: 陛下天姿至孝，喪逾三年，言及隕涕，雖曾、閔不過也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heaven-given nature supremely filial; mourning exceeded three years; speaking of it tears fell—even Zeng and Min were not more.
translations.idiomatic: Your filial mourning for the late emperor has exceeded three years and moves you to tears—Zengzi and Min Ziqian could do no more.

sentences.zh: 敬賢任才，使之盡力，有逾成、康。

translations.literal: Respecting worthies and employing talent, causing them to exhaust strength—surpasses Cheng and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: You honor the worthy and use talent to the full—more than Cheng and Kang achieved.

sentences.zh: 故國內和一，大小戮力，臣所不能陳。

translations.literal: Therefore within the state united as one, great and small join strength—what your servant cannot set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom is united and all ranks strive together—more than your servant can praise.

sentences.zh: 然臣不勝大願，願復廣人所不能者。

translations.literal: Yet your servant cannot overcome a great wish: I wish again to broaden what others cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I beg you to go further where others fall short.

sentences.zh: 夫挽大重者，其用力苦不眾，拔大艱者，其善術苦不廣，且承事宗廟者，非徒求福祐，所以率民尊上也。

translations.literal: Now he who pulls great weight—his using force bitterly lacks multitude; he who uproots great hardship—his good art bitterly lacks breadth; moreover those who undertake service to the ancestral temple do not only seek blessing and protection—it is thereby to lead the people to honor the high.
translations.idiomatic: Great burdens need many hands; great crises need broad counsel. Tending the ancestral shrines is not only for blessing—it teaches the people to honor their ruler.

sentences.zh: 至於四時之祀，或有不臨，池苑之觀；

translations.literal: As to the four seasons' sacrifices, sometimes there is not attendance; viewing of pools and parks;
translations.idiomatic: Yet sometimes you miss the seasonal sacrifices or visit the parks and pools;

sentences.zh: 或有仍出，臣之愚滯，私不自安。

translations.literal: sometimes there is still going out—your servant's foolish dullness, privately cannot be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: your servant is troubled in private.

sentences.zh: 夫憂責在身者，不暇盡樂，先帝之志，堂構未成，誠非盡樂之時。

translations.literal: Now he who bears care and duty on his person has no leisure for full joy; the First Sovereign's intent, hall and frame not yet completed—truly this is not a time for full joy.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler with heavy cares cannot indulge every pleasure; the late emperor’s work is unfinished—this is no time for revelry.

sentences.zh: 願省減樂官、後宮所增造，但奉備先帝所施，下為子孫節儉之教。

translations.literal: I wish you to reduce and cut musicians and rear palace's additions, only uphold what the First Sovereign established, below give sons and grandsons frugal teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Please cut the music bureau and new palace building, keep only what the late emperor left, and teach your heirs thrift by example.

sentences.zh: 徙為中散大夫，猶侍太子。

translations.literal: Transferred to grandee at leisure, still attended the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to grandee at leisure but still attended the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 於時軍旅數出，百姓凋瘁，周與尚書令陳祗論其利害，退而書之，謂之《仇國論》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: At that time armies repeatedly went out, the hundred surnames withered; Zhou with Masters of Writing Ling Chen Zhi discussed its benefit and harm, withdrew and wrote it, calling it the Discourse on Rival States; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: As armies marched often and the people grew exhausted, Qiao Zhou debated policy with director of the secretariat Chen Zhi and wrote the Discourse on Rival States. It begins:

sentences.zh: 因餘之國小，而肇建之國大，並爭於世而為仇敵。

translations.literal: The state Remnant-of-Yin was small, while the state Newly-Founded was large; together they strove in the age and became rival foes.
translations.idiomatic: A small state called Remnant-of-Yin and a large state called Newly-Founded contended as enemies in the world.

sentences.zh: 因餘之國有高賢卿者，問於伏愚子曰：「今國事未定，上下勞心，往古之事，能以弱勝強者，其術何如？

translations.literal: In Remnant-of-Yin there was one called High Worthy Minister, who asked Folly-Hidden Master saying, "Now state affairs are not settled; above and below labor in heart; in affairs of past ages, those able with weak to overcome strong—what was their art?"
translations.idiomatic: A minister of Remnant-of-Yin asked the Master Folly-Hidden how, in ancient times, the weak had overcome the strong while the state was still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 」伏愚子曰：「吾聞之，處大無患者恆多慢，處小有憂者恆思善；

translations.literal: " Folly-Hidden Master said, "I have heard: those placed great without calamity always much slacken; those placed small with worry always think on good;
translations.idiomatic: The master replied that great powers without danger grow careless, while small states in peril think of improvement.

sentences.zh: 多慢則生亂，恩善則生治，理之常也。

translations.literal: Much slackening then produces chaos; thinking good then produces order—this is principle's constant.
translations.idiomatic: Sloth breeds disorder and care for good brings order—that is the constant way.

sentences.zh: 故周文養民，以少取多；

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen of Zhou nurtured the people, with few took many;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen nourished the people and with few conquered many;

sentences.zh: 勾踐卹眾，以弱斃強，此其術也。

translations.literal: Goujian pitied the host, with weak killed strong—this was their art."
translations.idiomatic: Goujian comforted his troops and destroyed a strong foe with a weak one—that was their method."

sentences.zh: 」賢卿曰：「囊者項強漢弱，相與戰爭，無日寧息，然項羽與漢約分鴻溝為界，各欲歸息民；

translations.literal: " Worthy Minister said, "In the past Xiang was strong and Han weak; mutually they warred, no day peaceful rest; yet Xiang Yu with Han covenanted to divide at Hong Canal as border, each wished to return and rest the people;
translations.idiomatic: The minister objected that Xiang Yu and Liu Bang had fought endlessly until they agreed to divide at the Hong Canal and rest their peoples.

sentences.zh: 張良以為民志既定，則難動也，尋帥追羽，終斃項氏，豈必由文王之事乎？

translations.literal: Zhang Liang thought the people's will already fixed, then hard to move; soon led troops pursuing Yu, in the end killed off the Xiang clan—did it have to follow King Wen's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang held that once hearts were set they were hard to shift; Han then pursued Yu and destroyed him—need that follow King Wen’s patient path?"

sentences.zh: 肇建之國方有疾疢，我因其隙，陷其邊陲，覬增其疾而斃之也。

translations.literal: Newly-Founded's state just had sickness; I exploit its gap, sink into its border marches, hope to increase its sickness and kill it.
translations.idiomatic: Newly-Founded is already sick; we should strike its borders, worsen its illness, and finish it.

sentences.zh: 」伏愚子曰：「當殷、周之際，王候世尊，君臣久固，民習所專；

translations.literal: " Folly-Hidden Master said, "At the Yin-Zhou transition, kings and marquises generation honored, ruler and minister long firm, the people practiced what they were devoted to;
translations.idiomatic: The master answered that in the Yin–Zhou age lords had long ruled and the people were set in their ways;

sentences.zh: 深根者難拔，據固者難遷。

translations.literal: Deep-rooted is hard to uproot; firmly based is hard to shift.
translations.idiomatic: deep roots are hard to tear up and strong positions hard to dislodge.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，雖漢祖安能杖劍鞭馬而取天下乎？

translations.literal: At this time, even Han's Ancestor how could he staff sword whip horse and take the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Even Gaozu could not have seized the realm by sword and horse then."

sentences.zh: 當秦罷候置守之後，民疲秦役，天下土崩；

translations.literal: When Qin abolished marquises and set guardians afterward, the people were weary of Qin's corvée; the realm earth-collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: After Qin replaced feudal lords with governors, the people broke under its labor and the realm crumbled;

sentences.zh: 或歲改主，或月易公，鳥驚獸駭，莫知所從，於是豪強並爭，虎裂狼分，疾搏者獲多，遲後者見吞。

translations.literal: some years changed lord, some months exchanged duke; birds startled beasts frightened, none knew what to follow; then heroes together strove, tiger-torn wolf-divided; swift strikers got much, late followers were swallowed.
translations.idiomatic: rulers changed yearly or monthly, folk fled like startled birds, and strongmen tore the map apart—the quick swallowed the slow.

sentences.zh: 今我與肇建皆傳國易世矣，既非秦末鼎沸之時，實有六國並據之勢，故可為文王，難為漢祖。

translations.literal: Now I and Newly-Founded both have transmitted states and changed generations; it is already not Qin end cauldron-boiling time, but truly has the Six States' parallel-holding situation—therefore one can be King Wen, hard to be Han's Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: We and Newly-Founded are established states, not the free-for-all at Qin’s fall; the situation resembles the Warring States—one may play King Wen, not Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 夫民疲勞，則騷擾之兆生，上慢下暴則瓦解之形起。

translations.literal: When the people are weary and toiled, then omens of disturbance arise; when above is slack and below cruel, then forms of tile-shattering rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are worn out, unrest appears; when the ruler is arrogant and the ruled harsh, collapse follows.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『射幸數跌，不如審發。

translations.literal: The proverb says: 'Archery lucky—many misses; not like careful release.'
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says: hasty shots often miss; better to aim once with care.'

sentences.zh: 』是故智者不為小利移目，不為意似改步，時可而後動，數合而後舉，故湯、武之師不再戰而克，誠重民勞而度時審也。

translations.literal: ' Therefore the wise do not for small profit shift the eye, do not for seeming intention change step; when the season permits then afterward move, when the count matches then afterward raise—therefore Tang and Wu's hosts did not twice fight yet conquered; truly they valued people's toil and measured the season carefully.
translations.idiomatic: So the wise ignore small bait and false openings, strike when the time and omens align, and Tang and Wu won without a second battle because they spared the people and judged the moment.

sentences.zh: 如遂極武黜征，土崩勢生，不幸遇難，雖有智者將不能謀之矣；

translations.literal: If then exhaust martial force and dismiss campaigns, earth-collapse momentum arises; if unluckily meet disaster, though there be a wise man he will not be able to plan it;
translations.idiomatic: If you press military force to the limit, collapse follows; when disaster strikes, no wit can save you;

sentences.zh: 若乃奇變縱橫，出入無間，沖波截轍，超谷越山，不由舟楫而濟盟津者，我愚子也，實所不及。」

translations.literal: As for strange shifts crisscross, in-out without gap, dashing waves cutting wheel-tracks, leaping valleys crossing mountains, not by boat and oar yet crossing Meng Ford—I am a foolish child; truly what I cannot reach."
translations.idiomatic: as for lightning raids across rivers and mountains without boats—that is beyond a dullard like me."

sentences.zh: 後遷光祿大夫，位亞九列。

translations.literal: Later promoted grandee grand of the household, rank next below the nine rows.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to grandee grand of the household, just below the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 周雖不與政事，以儒行見禮。

translations.literal: Although Zhou did not join government affairs, by Confucian conduct he was shown ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Though he took no part in administration, he was honored for his Confucian conduct.

sentences.zh: 時訪大議，輒據經以對，而後生好事者亦諮問所疑焉。

translations.literal: When consulted on great debate, always cited the classics to answer; and later-born lovers of affairs also consulted what they doubted.
translations.idiomatic: When great questions arose he answered from the classics, and younger scholars brought him their doubts.

sentences.zh: 景耀六年冬，魏大將軍鄧艾克江由，長驅而前。

translations.literal: In winter of the sixth year of Jingyao, Wei Grand General Deng Ai took Jiangyou and drove straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 263 Wei general-in-chief Deng Ai took Jiangyou and drove deep into Shu.

sentences.zh: 而蜀本謂敵不便至，不作城守調度。

translations.literal: But Shu originally thought the enemy would not easily arrive, did not make city defense arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had assumed the foe would not come so soon and had not prepared the defenses.

sentences.zh: 及聞艾已人陰平，百姓擾擾，皆進山野，不可禁制。

translations.literal: When they heard Ai had already entered Yinping, the hundred surnames were in turmoil, all fled into mountain wilds, could not be forbidden and controlled.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Deng Ai had entered Yinping, the people panicked and fled to the hills beyond control.
