sentences.zh: 後主使臣羣會議，計無所出。

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign sent ministers and host to meet and deliberate; plans came out from nowhere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called his ministers; no plan emerged.

sentences.zh: 或以為蜀之與吳，本為和國，宜可奔吳；

translations.literal: Some thought Shu with Wu, originally were allied states—it would be right to flee to Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Some said Shu and Wu were allies and the court should flee east;

sentences.zh: 或以為南中七郡，阻險鬥絕，易以自守，宜可奔南。

translations.literal: some thought the south center seven commanderies, blocked by precipices and cut off, easy thereby to self-defend—it would be right to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: others urged flight to the seven southern commanderies, whose defiles were easy to hold.

sentences.zh: 惟周以為：

translations.literal: Only Zhou thought:
translations.idiomatic: Only Qiao Zhou argued:

sentences.zh: 自古以來，無寄他國為天子者也，今若入吳，固當臣服。

translations.literal: From antiquity to now, there has been none who lodged in another state as Son of Heaven; now if you enter Wu, solidly you ought to submit as subject.
translations.idiomatic: No emperor has ever taken refuge in another state as an equal; if you go to Wu you must submit as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 且政理不殊，則大能吞小，此數之自然也。

translations.literal: Moreover where government order is not different, then the great can swallow the small—this is number's naturalness.
translations.idiomatic: Where government is alike, the greater swallows the lesser—that is fate’s way.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，則魏能並吳，吳不能並魏明矣。

translations.literal: From this speaking, then Wei can annex Wu; Wu cannot annex Wei—clear.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Wei can absorb Wu, but Wu cannot absorb Wei—this is plain.

sentences.zh: 等為小稱臣，孰與為大？

translations.literal: Equal as small calling yourself subject—how does it compare to being great?
translations.idiomatic: Better to yield once to the great power than twice to the small.

sentences.zh: 再辱之恥，何與一辱？

translations.literal: Twice-shamed's disgrace—how does it compare to one shame?
translations.idiomatic: A second humiliation is worse than one.

sentences.zh: 且若欲奔南，則當早為之計，然後可果；

translations.literal: Moreover if you wish to flee south, then ought early to make the plan, afterward can be firm;
translations.idiomatic: Flight south required long planning to succeed;

sentences.zh: 今大敵以近，禍敗將及，羣小之心，無一可保，恐發足之日，其變不測，何至南之有乎！

translations.literal: now great enemy is near, calamity and defeat about to arrive; petty men's hearts—none can be trusted; I fear the day you set foot, their changes cannot be fathomed—what reaching south is there!
translations.idiomatic: now disaster is at hand and small men cannot be trusted; the moment you move, mutiny may strike—how would you ever reach the south!

sentences.zh: 羣臣或難周曰：「今艾以不遠，恐不受降，如之何？

translations.literal: Some ministers challenged Zhou saying, "Now Ai is not far—I fear he will not accept surrender—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Some objected that Deng Ai was near and might refuse surrender.

sentences.zh: 」周曰：「方今東吳未賓，事勢不得不受之，受之後，不得不禮。

translations.literal: " Zhou said, "Just now eastern Wu has not submitted; the situation forces them to accept it; after accepting, they must show ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou replied that eastern Wu had not yet submitted to Wei, so Wei must accept a surrender from Shu and would have to treat the ruler with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 若陛下降魏，魏不裂土以封陛下者，周請身詣京都，以古義爭之。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty submits to Wei, and Wei does not split land to enfeoff Your Majesty, Zhou requests personally to go to the capital, with ancient righteousness to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: If Wei failed to enfeoff Your Majesty, I would go myself to Luoyang and argue the classical precedents.

sentences.zh: 」眾人無以易周之理。

translations.literal: " The host had nothing to change Zhou's reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: No one could refute him.

sentences.zh: 後主猶疑於入南，周上疏曰：

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign still doubted about entering south; Zhou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still hesitated over fleeing south; Qiao Zhou memorialized:

sentences.zh: 或說陛下以北兵深入，有欲適南之計，臣愚以為不安。

translations.literal: Someone told Your Majesty that northern troops deeply enter, and there is a plan to go south—your servant foolishly thinks it unsafe.
translations.idiomatic: Some have urged flight south before the northern army; your servant thinks that unsafe.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 南方遠夷之地，平常無所供為，猶數反叛，自丞相亮南征，兵勢逼之，窮乃幸從，是後供出官賦，取以給兵，以為愁怨，此患國之人也。

translations.literal: The south is far barbarian land; in ordinary times nothing supplied or done, still repeatedly rebelled; since Chancellor Liang's southern campaign, military power pressed them, in extremity then luckily followed; afterward supplying official taxes, taking to supply troops—they harbor resentment—this is a people who harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: The south is distant tribal country that even in peace often rebelled; only Zhuge Liang’s campaign forced submission, and since then taxes for the army have bred resentment—those are a disaffected people.

sentences.zh: 今以窮迫，欲往依恃，恐必復反叛，一也；

translations.literal: Now in extremity pressed, wishing to go rely on them—I fear they certainly will rebel again—first point;
translations.idiomatic: To flee there in desperation would likely spark new rebellion—first point;

sentences.zh: 北兵之來，非但取蜀而已，若奔南方，必因人勢衰，及時赴追，二也；

translations.literal: Northern troops' coming is not only to take Shu; if you flee south, they must follow men's power declining, in season hurry pursuit—second point;
translations.idiomatic: Wei aims beyond Shu; if you run south they will pursue your weakened force—second point;

sentences.zh: 若至南方，外當拒敵，內供服御，費用張廣，他無所取，耗損諸夷必甚，甚必速叛，三也；

translations.literal: If you reach south, outside must resist enemy, inside supply clothing and food—costs spread wide, elsewhere nothing to take; exhausting the various Yi must be severe; severe then surely swift rebellion—third point;
translations.idiomatic: There you would fight the enemy abroad and supply the court at home, bleeding the tribes until they revolt—third point;

sentences.zh: 昔王郎以邯鄲僭號，時世祖在信都，畏逼於郎，欲棄還關中。

translations.literal: Formerly Wang Lang with Handan usurped title; at the time the Shizu was at Xindu, feared pressure from Lang, wished to abandon and return to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lang seized Handan, Guangwu at Xindu feared him and thought of fleeing back to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 邳肜諫曰：『明公西還，則邯鄲城民不肯捐父母，背城主，而千里送公，其亡叛可必也。

translations.literal: Pi Tong remonstrated saying, 'If the enlightened lord returns west, then Handan city's people will not be willing to abandon parents, turn back on the city lord, yet send you a thousand li—their fleeing rebellion can be certain.'
translations.idiomatic: Pi Tong warned that if Guangwu withdrew west, the people of Handan would not abandon kin and lord to follow him a thousand li—they would surely desert.

sentences.zh: 』世祖從之，遂破邯鄲。

translations.literal: ' The Shizu followed it, thereupon broke Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu listened and took Handan.

sentences.zh: 今北兵至，陛下南行，誠恐邳肜之言覆信於今，四也。

translations.literal: Now northern troops arrive; Your Majesty goes south—I truly fear Pi Tong's words will repeat trust today—fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: If you flee south now, Pi Tong’s warning may come true again—fourth point.

sentences.zh: 願陛下早為之圖，可獲爵土；

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty early to plan for this—can obtain noble rank and land;
translations.idiomatic: Plan early and you may keep rank and a fief;

sentences.zh: 若遂適南，勢窮乃服，其禍必深。

translations.literal: if then go south, power exhausted then submit—the calamity must be deep.
translations.idiomatic: if you flee south and yield only at the last, the harm will be far worse.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『亢之為言，知而不知喪，知存而不知亡；

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'Excess's speaking is: knowing yet not knowing loss, knowing preservation yet not knowing perishing;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says of excess: to know gain but not loss, survival but not ruin;

sentences.zh: 知得失存亡而不失其正者，其惟聖人乎！

translations.literal: to know gain and loss, preservation and perishing yet not lose correctness—is it not only the sage!'
translations.idiomatic: to grasp rise and fall yet keep to the right—only a sage can do that!'

sentences.zh: 」言聖人知命而不苟必也，故堯，舜以子不善，知天有授，而求授人；

translations.literal: " It speaks of the sage knowing fate yet not rashly insisting; therefore Yao and Shun, because sons were not good, knew Heaven had a grant and sought to grant to others;
translations.idiomatic: The sage accepts Heaven’s mandate without stubborn pride; Yao and Shun passed the throne to worthies when their sons proved unfit;

sentences.zh: 子雖不肖，禍尚未萌，而迎綬於人，況禍以至乎！

translations.literal: sons although not worthy, calamity not yet sprouted, yet welcomed the cord from others—how much more when calamity has already arrived!
translations.idiomatic: they yielded before disaster struck—how much more should you when it is already here!

sentences.zh: 故微子以殷王之昆，面縛銜璧而歸武王，豈所樂哉，不得已也。

translations.literal: Therefore Weizi, as Yin king's elder brother, bound face and held jade in mouth to return to King Wu—was it what he delighted in? It was without choice.
translations.idiomatic: Weizi, brother of the last Yin king, bound himself and offered his jade to King Wu—not from joy but necessity.

sentences.zh: 於是遂從周策。

translations.literal: Thereupon they followed Zhou's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed Qiao Zhou’s advice.

sentences.zh: 劉氏無虞，一邦蒙賴，周之謀也。

translations.literal: The Liu house without peril, one state received reliance—this was Zhou's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Liu was spared and the state benefited by Qiao Zhou’s counsel.

sentences.zh: 〈孫綽評曰：譙周說後主降魏，可乎？

translations.literal: 〈Sun Chuo appraises saying: Qiao Zhou persuaded the Later Sovereign to submit to Wei—was it permissible?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo asks whether Qiao Zhou was right to urge the Later Ruler to surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 曰：自為天子而乞降請命，何恥之深乎！

translations.literal: It is said: From being Son of Heaven to begging surrender and seeking mandate—what depth of shame!
translations.idiomatic: He answers that for a Son of Heaven to beg for his life is the deepest shame.

sentences.zh: 夫為社稷死則死之，為社稷亡則亡之。

translations.literal: For the altars of soil and grain die then die; for the altars perish then perish.
translations.idiomatic: One should die for the altars or perish with them.

sentences.zh: 先君正魏之篡，不與同天矣。

translations.literal: The former lord rectified Wei's usurpation—not sharing the same sky.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor held Wei a usurper and would not share Heaven with it.

sentences.zh: 推過於其父，俛首而事讎，可謂苟存，豈大居正之道哉！

translations.literal: Pushing fault onto his father, bowing head to serve an enemy—may be called mere survival; how is it the great way of holding correctness!
translations.idiomatic: To shift blame to the father and bow to the foe is bare survival, not the way of rectitude.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：春秋之義，國君死社稷，卿大夫死位，況稱天子而可辱於人乎！

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: The Spring and Autumn's meaning—state lord dies for the altars, ministers die for their posts—how much more one titled Son of Heaven can be humiliated by others!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng cites the Spring and Autumn: a ruler dies for his altars and ministers for their posts—how can a Son of Heaven suffer humiliation!

sentences.zh: 周謂萬乘之君偷生苟免，亡禮希利，要冀微榮，惑矣。

translations.literal: Zhou deemed a lord of ten thousand chariots stealing life and seeking bare escape, losing ritual and hoping for profit, grasping at slight glory—deluded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng calls Qiao Zhou deluded for urging a great king to cling to life, abandon ritual, and grasp petty advantage.

sentences.zh: 且以事勢言之，理有未盡。

translations.literal: Moreover by affairs and situation speaking of it, the principle has not been exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on the facts of the case, the argument is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 禪雖庸主，實無桀、紂之酷，戰雖屢北，未有土崩之亂，縱不能君臣固守，背城借一，自可退次東鄙以思後圖。

translations.literal: Shan although a mediocre lord, truly had no Jie or Zhou's cruelty; though battles often north, there was not yet earth-collapse chaos; even if unable ruler and ministers firmly to hold, back to the city borrow one stroke, naturally could withdraw and encamp east march to plan later.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan was a mediocre ruler, not a Jie or Zhou; though defeated often, the state had not collapsed; even without a last-ditch defense of the capital, he could have withdrawn eastward and planned recovery.

sentences.zh: 是時羅憲以重兵據白帝，霍弋以強卒鎮夜郎。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Xian with heavy troops held Baidi, Huo Yi with strong soldiers garrisoned Yelang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian still held Baidi with a strong force and Huo Yi garrisoned the south at Yelang.

sentences.zh: 蜀土險狹，山水峻隔，絕巘激湍，非步卒所涉。

translations.literal: Shu soil is precipitous and narrow; mountains and waters steeply block; sheer cliffs and rushing torrents—not what foot soldiers can cross.
translations.idiomatic: Shu is rugged: cliffs and rapids bar the way—not ground for infantry alone.

sentences.zh: 若悉取舟楫，保據江州，徵兵南中，乞師東國，如此則姜、廖五將自然雲從，吳之三師承命電赴，何投寄之無所而慮於必亡邪？

translations.literal: If you gathered all boats and oars, secured and held Jiangzhou, raised troops in the south center, begged troops from the eastern state—thus then Jiang, Liao and the five generals naturally cloud-followed, Wu's three hosts receiving orders lightning-hurried—what lack of place to cast reliance that you should worry of certain perishing?
translations.idiomatic: Had he seized the river fleet, held Jiangzhou, mobilized the south, and begged aid from Wu, Jiang Wei and the other generals would have rallied, Wu’s armies would have sped to help—where was the need to think only of surrender?

sentences.zh: 魏師之來，褰國大舉，欲追則舟楫靡資，欲留則師老多虞。

translations.literal: Wei army's coming, raising the state in full force—if wishing to pursue then boats and oars lack supply; if wishing to remain then army ages with many worries.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had mobilized the whole realm: to pursue lacked boats; to stay risked a weary army.

sentences.zh: 且屈伸有會，情勢代起，徐因思奮之民，以攻驕惰之卒，此越王所以敗闔閭，田單所以摧騎劫也，何為匆匆遽自囚虜，下堅壁於敵人，致斫石之至恨哉？

translations.literal: Moreover bending and stretching have their meetings; feeling and situation rise in turn; slowly using people who long to rise, to attack arrogant lazy soldiers—this is how the Yue king defeated Helü, how Tian Dan crushed Qi Jie—why hastily hasten to bind yourself captive, cast a firm wall to the enemy, incur utmost hatred of hacking stone?
translations.idiomatic: Fortunes turn: patient use of a willing populace against arrogant troops was how Goujian beat Helü and Tian Dan broke the Yan siege—why rush to captivity and earn eternal shame?

sentences.zh: 葛生有云：「事之不濟則已耳，安能復為之下！

translations.literal: The Ge Sheng has a saying: 'If affairs do not succeed, then stop—how can again serve beneath them!'
translations.idiomatic: The poem Ge Sheng says: if the cause fails, so be it—how could one serve beneath the victor again!

sentences.zh: 」壯哉斯言，可以立懦夫之志矣。

translations.literal: " How bold this saying—it can establish a coward's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Noble words—they could steel the faint-hearted.

sentences.zh: 觀古燕、齊、荊、越之敗，或國覆主滅，或魚縣鳥竄，終能建功立事，康復社稷，豈曰天助，抑亦人謀也。

translations.literal: Observe ancient Yan, Qi, Jing, Yue's defeats—some state overturned lord extinguished, some fish-hung bird-scattered; in the end able to establish merit and affairs, restore the altars—can one say heaven aided? Or also human planning.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Qi, Chu, and Yue sometimes fell utterly, sometimes scattered like fish and birds, yet later restored their houses by human effort, not fate alone.

sentences.zh: 向使懷苟存之計，納譙周之言，何邦基之能構，令名之可獲哉？

translations.literal: If formerly one had embraced mere-survival's plan, accepted Qiao Zhou's words—what founding of state foundation could be built, what fair name could be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Had they clung to survival and heeded Qiao Zhou, what foundation or fair fame could ever have been won?

sentences.zh: 禪既闇主，周實駑臣，方之申包、田單、范蠡、大夫種，不亦遠乎！〉

translations.literal: Shan already a dark lord, Zhou truly a dull minister—compared to Shen Baoxu, Tian Dan, Fan Li, Grand Officer Zhong—is it not far!〉
translations.idiomatic: A dim emperor and a plodding minister—how far from Shen Baoxu, Tian Dan, Fan Li, or Wen Zhong!〉

sentences.zh: 時晉文王為魏相國，以周有全國之功，封陽城亭侯。

translations.literal: At the time Jin King Wen was Wei chancellor of state; because Zhou had merit of preserving the whole state, enfeoffed him Marquis of Yangcheng village.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao was Wei’s chancellor, he enfeoffed Qiao Zhou as village marquis of Yangcheng for saving the realm.

sentences.zh: 又下書辟周，周發至漢中，困疾不進。

translations.literal: Again issued summons to Zhou; Zhou set out and reached Hanzhong, blocked by illness did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again but fell ill at Hanzhong and went no farther.

sentences.zh: 咸熙二年夏，巴郡文立從洛陽還蜀，過見周。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year of Xianxi, Wen Li of Ba commandery from Luoyang returned to Shu, passing visited Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 265 Wen Li of Ba, returning from Luoyang to Shu, visited Qiao Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周語次，因書版示立曰：「典午忽兮，月酉沒兮。

translations.literal: Zhou in conversation, then wrote on a board to show Li saying: 'The Director of Noon passes suddenly; the moon in you sets.'
translations.idiomatic: In conversation Qiao Zhou wrote on a slip for Wen Li: the word for Sima portends sudden change; the month you means the eighth month will see an end.

sentences.zh: 」典午者謂司馬也，月酉者謂八月也，至八月而文王果崩。

translations.literal: " Director of Noon means Sima; moon in you means eighth month; reaching the eighth month King Wen indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The riddle meant the house of Sima and the eighth month; Sima Zhao died that August as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：文立字廣休，少治毛詩、三禮，兼通羣書。

translations.literal: 〈The Huayang guo zhi states: Li's courtesy name Guangxiu; in youth worked Mao Odes and three Rites, concurrently penetrated many books.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang guo zhi names Wen Li Guangxiu, trained in the Mao Odes and three Rites and widely read.

sentences.zh: 刺史費禕命為從事，入為尚書郎，復辟禕大將軍東曹掾，稍遷尚書。

translations.literal: Inspector Fei Yi appointed him staff aide; entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing; again summoned as Grand General Yi's eastern bureau clerk; gradually promoted Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi as governor made him a staff aide; he rose to gentleman of the secretariat, then clerk in Fei Yi’s eastern bureau as general-in-chief, and finally master of writing.

sentences.zh: 蜀並於魏，梁州建，首為別駕從事，舉秀才。

translations.literal: Shu was annexed by Wei; Liangzhou was established; first became aide-de-camp, nominated flourishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he became chief aide when Liangzhou was set up and was nominated flourishing talent.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始二年，拜濟陰太守，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In Jin's second year of Taishi, appointed Administrator of Jiyin, promoted palace attendant to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In 266 he became governor of Jiyin and then palace attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 立上言：「故蜀大官及盡忠死事者子孫，雖仕郡國，或有不才，同之齊民為劇；

translations.literal: Li submitted saying: 'Former Shu great officers and those who died in loyal service—their descendants, although serving commanderies and principalities, some lacking talent, treating them same as common folk is harsh;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Li memorialized that descendants of Shu’s high officials and loyal dead, even if mediocre in local posts, should not be burdened like commoners;

sentences.zh: 又諸葛亮、蔣琬、費禕等子孫流徙中畿，各宜量才敘用，以慰巴、蜀之心，傾吳人之望。

translations.literal: again Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi and others' descendants drifted to the central domain—each ought to be employed according to talent, to console Ba and Shu's hearts, to incline Wu people's hopes.'
translations.idiomatic: and that the exiled kin of Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and others should be placed by merit to reassure Ba–Shu and impress Wu.

sentences.zh: 」事皆施行。

translations.literal: " The matters were all carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍，獻可替否，多所補納。

translations.literal: Transferred gentleman attendant at leisure, offering what was fit and replacing what was not—much supplemented and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: As gentleman attendant at leisure he remonstrated effectively and many of his suggestions were accepted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷衛尉，中朝服其賢雅，為時名卿。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted commandant of the guards; the central court submitted to his worthy refinement, became a famed minister of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commandant of the guards and was honored at court as a leading minister.

sentences.zh: 咸寧末卒。

translations.literal: Died at the end of Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of the Xianning era.

sentences.zh: 立章奏詩詩賦論頌凡數十篇。〉

translations.literal: Li memorials, poems, poems, fu, discourses, and eulogies in all several tens of pieces.〉
translations.idiomatic: His memorials, poems, fu, treatises, and eulogies numbered several dozen.〉

sentences.zh: 晉室踐阼，累下詔所在發遣周。

translations.literal: The Jin house ascended the throne; repeatedly issued edicts to the places to dispatch Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin accession, repeated edicts ordered local authorities to send Qiao Zhou to court.

sentences.zh: 周遂輿疾詣洛，泰始三年至。

translations.literal: Zhou then rode illness and went to Luoyang; in the third year of Taishi arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Luoyang in a litter, ill, and arrived in 267.

sentences.zh: 以疾不起，就拜騎都尉，周乃自陳無功而封，求還爵土，皆不聽許。

translations.literal: Because of illness did not rise; thereupon appointed chief of cavalry; Zhou then self-stated without merit yet enfeoffed, begged to return rank and fief—all not listened and permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Too sick to rise, he received appointment as chief of cavalry at his bedside; he pleaded that he had earned no title and asked to surrender his rank and fief, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 五年，予常為本郡中正，清定事訖，求休還家，往與周別。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, I once was local commandery rectifier; when the clarification and fixing affairs finished, begged leave to return home, went to part from Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 269, after I had finished my stint as rectifier of my commandery and took leave to return home, I visited Qiao Zhou to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 周語予曰：「昔孔子七十二、劉向、楊雄七十一而沒，今吾年過七十，庶慕孔子遺風，可與劉、楊同軌，恐不出後歲，必便長逝，不復相見矣。

translations.literal: Zhou spoke to me saying: 'Formerly Confucius at seventy-two, Liu Xiang, Yang Xiong at seventy-one then died; now my years pass seventy; perhaps I admire Confucius' surviving wind, can with Liu, Yang share the track—fear not beyond the next year, certainly then long depart, not again meet.'
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou told me: Confucius died at seventy-two, Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong at seventy-one; I am past seventy and hope to follow Confucius’s example and match Liu and Yang in span—but I fear I shall not see another year, and we will not meet again.

sentences.zh: 」疑周以術知之，假而此言也。

translations.literal: " I suspected Zhou by technique knew it, borrowing and this speech.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect he divined his end and framed it in those words.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，為散騎常侍，疾篤不拜，至冬卒。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year, made gentleman attendant at leisure; illness grave did not assume office; reaching winter died.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 270 he was named gentleman attendant at leisure but was too ill to take office; he died that winter.

sentences.zh: 〈《晉陽秋》載詔曰：「朕甚悼之，賜朝服一具，衣一襲，錢十五萬。

translations.literal: 〈The Jin Yang qiu records an edict saying: 'I greatly mourn him; grant court robes one set, clothes one suit, cash one hundred fifty thousand.'
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Yang qiu records an edict: I mourn him deeply; grant one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, and 150,000 cash.

sentences.zh: 」周息熙上言，周臨終屬熙曰：「久抱疾，未曾朝見，若國恩賜朝服衣物者，勿以加身。

translations.literal: " Zhou's son Xi submitted saying: Zhou at end entrusted Xi saying: 'Long held illness, never had audience; if state's grace grants court robes and clothes, do not use them on the body.'
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao Xi reported that on his deathbed Qiao Zhou had said: I was long ill and never attended court; if the state sends court dress or garments, do not dress my corpse in them.

sentences.zh: 當還舊墓，道險行難，豫作輕棺。

translations.literal: Ought return to old tomb; road perilous travel hard; beforehand make light coffin.
translations.idiomatic: I am to lie in my old grave; the way is rough, so prepare a light coffin in advance.

sentences.zh: 殯斂已畢，上還所賜。

translations.literal: When laying-out and encoffining already finished, submit return what was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites, return the imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 」詔還衣服，給棺直。〉

translations.literal: " Edict returned the clothes, supplied coffin expense.〉
translations.idiomatic: The court took back the clothes but paid for the coffin.〉

sentences.zh: 凡所著述，擇定《法訓》、《五經論》、《古史考》書之屬百餘篇。

translations.literal: In all what he wrote and composed, selected and fixed the Fa xun, Wu jing lun, Gu shi kao and books of that sort over one hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His writings, including the finalized Fa xun, Discourses on the Five Classics, Examination of Ancient History, and similar works, numbered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆舊傳曰：益州刺史董榮圖畫周像於州學，命從事李通頌之曰：「抑抑譙侯，好古述儒，寶道懷真，鑑世盈虛，雅名美跡，終始是書。

translations.literal: 〈The Yi bu ji jiu zhuan states: Inspector of Yi Province Dong Rong painted Zhou's likeness at the provincial school, ordered staff aide Li Tong to eulogize saying: 'Stately Marquis of Qiao, loves antiquity and transmits Ru learning, treasures the Way and embraces truth, mirrors the age's fullness and emptiness; elegant name and fair traces, from first to last are written.'
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Notables of Yi say that Governor Dong Rong had Qiao Zhou’s portrait painted at the provincial school and ordered aide Li Tong to compose a eulogy: stately lord of Qiao, lover of antiquity and teacher of the Ru, who treasured the Way and read the rise and fall of the age—his noble name and deeds are recorded from first to last.

sentences.zh: 我後欽賢，無言不譽，攀諸前哲，丹青是圖。

translations.literal: Our later ruler esteems worthies; no word not praise; climb to former wise ones; cinnabar and green thus pictured.
translations.idiomatic: Our ruler honors the worthy and praises without stint; he follows the sages of old and sets their images in paint.

sentences.zh: 嗟爾來葉，鑑茲顯模。」〉

translations.literal: Alas you later leaves, mirror this bright model.'"〉
translations.idiomatic: O posterity, take this shining example as your mirror.'"〉

sentences.zh: 孫 譙秀

translations.literal: Grandson Qiao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Qiao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 周三子，熙、賢、同，少子同頗好周業，亦以忠篤質素為行，舉孝廉，除錫令、東宮洗馬，召不就。

translations.literal: Zhou had three sons, Xi, Xian, Tong; the youngest son Tong quite loved Zhou's learning, also by loyal solid plain simplicity as conduct, nominated filial and incorrupt, appointed Magistrate of Xi, Eastern Palace groom, summoned did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou had three sons—Xi, Xian, and Tong. The youngest, Tong, followed his father’s studies and was known for steadfast simplicity; nominated filial and incorrupt, he was named magistrate of Xi and groom of the eastern palace but declined appointment when summoned.

sentences.zh: 〈周長子熙。

translations.literal: 〈Zhou's eldest son Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou’s eldest son was Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙子秀，字元彥。

translations.literal: Xi's son Xiu, courtesy name Yuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi’s son Xiu bore the courtesy name Yuanyan.

sentences.zh: 《晉陽秋》曰：秀性清靜，不交於世，知將大亂，豫絕人事，從兄弟及諸親裡不與相見。

translations.literal: The Jin Yang qiu states: Xiu's nature was clear and quiet; did not mingle with the world; knew there would be great chaos; beforehand cut off human affairs; cousins and all close kin in the village did not meet with one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Yang qiu says Xiu was reclusive, foresaw turmoil, and cut ties—even with cousins and neighbors he would not meet.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟命，及李雄盜蜀，安車徵秀，又雄叔父驤、驤子壽辟命，皆不應。

translations.literal: Commanderies and principalities summoned; when Li Xiong usurped Shu, comfort carriage summoned Xiu; again Xiong's uncle Xiang, Xiang's son Shou summoned—all did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored summons from local authorities; when Li Xiong seized Shu, Li sent a carriage for him, as did Li’s uncle Li Xiang and cousin Li Shou—he answered none of them.

sentences.zh: 常冠鹿皮，躬耕山藪。

translations.literal: Constantly capped in deerskin, personally plowed mountain marsh.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a deerskin cap and farmed the mountain wilds with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 永和三年，安西將軍桓溫平蜀，表薦秀曰：「臣聞大樸既虧，則高尚之標顯；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghe, General Who Guards the West Huan Wen pacified Shu, memorial recommended Xiu saying: 'Your subject has heard: when great simplicity is already damaged, then the mark of the lofty shines;
translations.idiomatic: In 347 General Huan Wen, having conquered Shu, memorialized: I have heard that when primal simplicity is lost, the banner of the high-minded stands forth;

sentences.zh: 道喪時昏，則忠貞之義彰。

translations.literal: When the Way is lost and the age is dark, then the meaning of loyalty and steadfastness shines forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way wanes and the times grow dark, loyalty and integrity shine the brighter.

sentences.zh: 故有洗耳投淵以振玄邈之風，亦有秉心矯跡以惇在三之節。

translations.literal: Therefore there are those who washed their ears and cast themselves into the depths to rouse the wind of the dark remote; there are also those who grasped their hearts and straightened their tracks to thicken integrity toward the threefold bond.
translations.idiomatic: Hence some washed their ears and leapt into rivers to revive a transcendent ethos, while others set their hearts and deeds to honor the threefold bond of kin and ruler.

sentences.zh: 是以上代之君，莫不崇重斯軌，所以篤俗訓民，靜一流競。

translations.literal: Therefore the lords of former ages all honored and weighted this path—thereby to make custom solid, instruct the people, quiet the restless, and stop contention.
translations.idiomatic: Past kings all honored this path to steady custom, teach the people, and calm reckless striving.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大晉應符禦世，運無常通，時有屯蹇，神州丘墟，三方圮裂，兔罝絕響於中林，白駒無聞於空谷，斯有識之所悼心，大雅之所嘆息者也。

translations.literal: I humbly consider: Great Jin responds to the tally and governs the age—fortune has no constant smoothness; times have blockage and hardship; the divine continent is mound and ruin; the three regions split and crack; the rabbit-snare falls silent in the central grove; the white colt goes unheard in the empty valley—this is what the knowing mourn in heart, what the great elegance sighs over.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin rules by mandate, yet fortune turns; the heartland lies in ruins and the realm is torn; worthy men no longer answer the hunt or emerge from seclusion—this grieves every thoughtful mind and every voice of conscience.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德嗣興，方恢天緒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagely virtue succeeds and rises; just now expanding heaven's thread.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty’s sacred virtue renews the line of Heaven and widens its design.

sentences.zh: 臣昔奉役，有事西土，鯨鯢既縣，思宣大化；

translations.literal: Your subject formerly received service, had affairs in the western soil; the krakens already hung; thought to proclaim great transformation;
translations.idiomatic: When I campaigned in the west and the rebels were executed, I sought to spread your transforming influence;

sentences.zh: 訪諸故老，搜楊潛逸，庶武羅於羿、浞之墟，想王蠋於亡齊之境。

translations.literal: Visited various old elders, searched and raised hidden recluses—hoping for Wu Luo at Yi and Zhuo's ruins, thinking of Wang Zhuo at perished Qi's border.
translations.idiomatic: I consulted elders and sought hidden worthies, hoping to find a Wu Luo amid the ruins of tyranny and a Wang Zhuo for a fallen state.

sentences.zh: 竊聞巴西譙秀，植操貞固，抱德肥遁，揚清渭波。

translations.literal: I have heard in Baxi Qiao Xiu, planted conduct chaste and firm, embraced virtue and fat reclusion, raised clarity on Wei River's waves.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Qiao Xiu of Baxi is steadfast in principle, lives by virtue in withdrawal, and keeps his purity unsullied as the Wei.

sentences.zh: 於時皇極遘道消之會，羣黎蹈顛沛之艱，中華有顧瞻之哀，幽谷無遷喬之望；

translations.literal: At that time the august pole met the meeting of the Way's waning; the masses trod overturning and hardship's severity; central Hua had look-back sorrow; deep valleys had no hope of moving to tall trees;
translations.idiomatic: When the throne faltered and the Way waned, the people suffered exile; the heartland mourned its fate and no recluse thought of leaving the hills for office;

sentences.zh: 凶命屢招，姦威仍偪，身寄虎吻，危同朝露，而能抗節玉立，誓不降辱，杜門絕跡，不面偽庭，進免龔勝亡身之禍，退無薛方詭之譏；

translations.literal: Fierce summons repeatedly summoned; treacherous might still pressed; body lodged in tiger's maw; peril same as morning dew—yet able to resist integrity jade-stand, swear not to descend to humiliation, block door cut off tracks, not face false court—advance avoided Gong Sheng body-lost calamity, retreat had no Xue Fang deceit's ridicule;
translations.idiomatic: Though death beckoned and tyrants pressed, his life hung by a thread like dew at dawn, he held his integrity like jade, refused humiliation, shut his door, shunned the usurper’s court—thus he escaped Gong Sheng’s fate and incurred none of the mockery aimed at Xue Fang’s compromise;

sentences.zh: 雖園、綺之棲商、洛，管寧之默遼海，方之於秀，殆無以過。

translations.literal: Although Dongyuan and Qili's dwelling at Shang and Luo, Guan Ning's silence at Liaohai—set beside Xiu, probably nothing surpasses.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the Four Haos at Shang and Luo or Guan Ning’s silence by the sea, Qiao Xiu stands second to none.

sentences.zh: 於今西土，以為美談。

translations.literal: In the present western land, it is taken as fine talk.
translations.idiomatic: In the west today his story is told with admiration.

sentences.zh: 夫旌德禮賢，化道之所先，崇表殊節，聖哲之上務。

translations.literal: Now displaying virtue and honoring worthies is transformation's Way's first; exalting and marking rare integrity is sage wise men's upper task.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring virtue and welcoming the worthy come first in governing; lifting up uncommon integrity is the foremost duty of a sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 方今六合未康，豺狼當路，遺黎偷薄，義聲弗聞，益宜振起道義之徒，以敦流遁之弊。

translations.literal: Just now the six directions are not yet peaceful; jackals and wolves block the road; surviving people are petty and thin; righteous fame is not heard—more ought to rouse those of the Way and righteousness, to thicken the flowing-reclusion's harm.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still unsettled, the ruthless hold the roads, the people are demoralized, and little is heard of righteousness; the court should rouse men of principle to counter the rush into withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 若秀蒙薄帛之徵，足以鎮靜頹風，軌訓囂俗；

translations.literal: If Xiu receives thin-silk's summons, enough to calm and quiet collapsing wind, track and instruct clamorous custom;
translations.idiomatic: If Xiu were summoned with modest silks, it would steady a failing ethos and set a standard for a restless age;

sentences.zh: 幽遐仰流，九服知化矣。

translations.literal: Remote regions look up to the current; the nine domains will know transformation.
translations.idiomatic: the farthest corners would look to your example and the nine domains would feel your transforming sway.

sentences.zh: 」及蕭敬叛亂，避難宕渠川中，鄉人宗族馮依者以百數。

translations.literal: " When Xiao Jing rebelled, he fled for refuge into the Dangqu rivers; fellow villagers and kin who leaned on him numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Jing rose in revolt, he took refuge in the Dangqu river country; hundreds of clansmen and neighbors rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 秀年八十，眾人以其薦老，欲代之負擔，秀拒曰：「各有老弱，當先營救。

translations.literal: Xiu's age eighty; the crowd seeing him advanced in years wished to replace him in carrying burdens; Xiu refused saying: 'Each has old and weak—ought first to plan rescue.'
translations.idiomatic: At eighty the party wished to carry his pack for him, but he refused: 'Every family has frail members—tend to them first.'

sentences.zh: 吾氣力自足堪此，不以垂朽之年累諸君也。

translations.literal: My qi and strength are enough to bear this; I will not with dangling-decay years burden you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: My strength is still equal to the road; I will not burden you with these failing years.'

sentences.zh: 」後十餘年，卒於家。〉

translations.literal: " After more than ten years, died at home.〉
translations.idiomatic: He died at home more than a decade later.〉

sentences.zh: 郤正字令先，河南偃師人也。

translations.literal: Xi Zheng, courtesy name Lingxian, was a man of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng, courtesy name Lingxian, was a native of Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖父儉，靈帝末為益州刺史，為盜賊所殺。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jian, at the end of Emperor Ling was Inspector of Yi Province, was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi Jian served as inspector of Yi under Emperor Ling and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 會天下大亂，故正父揖因留蜀。

translations.literal: Meeting the realm great chaos, therefore Zheng's father Yi remained in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire fell into chaos, his father Xi Yi stayed in Shu.

sentences.zh: 揖為將軍孟達都督，隨達降魏，為中書令史。

translations.literal: Yi was General Meng Da's area commander; followed Da in surrendering to Wei, became Secretariat document clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yi was area commander under General Meng Da and followed him into Wei service as a clerk in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正本名纂。

translations.literal: Zheng's original name was Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had originally been named Zuan.

sentences.zh: 少以父死母嫁，單煢雙立，而安貧好學，博覽墳籍。

translations.literal: In youth because father died mother remarried, alone and solitary both stood; yet was content with poverty and loved learning, broadly viewed tomb texts.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned by his father’s death and his mother’s remarriage, he grew up alone yet poor, studious, and widely read in the classics.

sentences.zh: 弱冠能屬文，入為秘書吏，轉為令史，遷郎，至令。

translations.literal: At weak-crown able to compose texts; entered as secretariat clerk; transferred to document clerk; promoted gentleman; reached director.
translations.idiomatic: At coming of age he could write; he entered the palace secretariat as a clerk, rose to document clerk, gentleman, and finally director.

sentences.zh: 性淡於榮利，而尤耽意文章，自司馬、王、揚、班、傅、張、蔡之儔遺文篇賦，及當世美書善論，益部有者，則鑽鑿推求，略皆寓目。

translations.literal: His nature was bland toward glory and profit, yet especially sunk intent on literary pieces—from Sima, Wang, Yang, Ban, Fu, Zhang, Cai's sort surviving texts and fu, and the current age's fine writings and good discourses, whatever Yi region had, he bored and chiseled, pushed and sought, and in outline all lodged his eye.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for rank or gain but devoured literature, hunting down every essay and fu from Sima Xiangru through Cai Yong and every notable work current in Yi that he could find.

sentences.zh: 自在內職，與宦人黃皓比屋周旋，經三十年。

translations.literal: From the time in inner office, with eunuch Huang Hao neighboring-house circled, passed thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years in inner service he worked next door to the eunuch Huang Hao.

sentences.zh: 皓從微至貴，操弄威權，正既不為皓所愛，亦不為皓所憎，是以宮不過六百石，而免於憂患。

translations.literal: Hao from low to noble, grasped and played with awe and power; Zheng neither was by Hao loved, nor was by Hao hated—therefore office did not pass six hundred shi, yet was spared from worry and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: As Huang Hao rose from obscurity to wield power, Zheng was neither favored nor hated by him, so his rank never rose above six hundred shi but he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 依則先儒，假文見意，號曰：《釋譏》，其文繼於崔駰《達旨》。

translations.literal: Following then former Ru, borrowing text to show meaning, titled: Shi ji (Explaining Ridicule); its text continues after Cui Yan's Da zhi (Articulating the Aim).
translations.idiomatic: Following the example of earlier scholars, he used literary form to set forth his meaning in a work titled Explaining Ridicule, modeled on Cui Yan’s Articulating the Aim.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its phrasing says:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 或有譏余者曰：『聞之前記，夫事與時並，名與功偕，然則名之與事，前哲之急務也。

translations.literal: Someone ridiculing me said: 'Heard in former records: affairs go together with the age, name goes together with merit—then name and affairs are former wise men's urgent task.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone mocked me: 'The old books say that deeds ride the times and reputation rides merit; for the wise of old, name and achievement were everything.'

sentences.zh: 是故創製作範，匪時不立，流稱垂名，匪功不記，名必須功而乃顯，事亦俟時以行止，身沒名滅，君子所恥。

translations.literal: Therefore creating and making models, not the time then not established; flowing title hanging name, not merit then not recorded; name must await merit then is manifest; affairs also wait for the time to act or stop; body gone name extinguished—what the gentleman shames.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions take shape only when the moment is right; fame endures only when tied to real deeds; when life ends and the name vanishes, the gentleman counts it shame.

sentences.zh: 是以達人研道，探頤索微，觀天運之符表，考人事之盛衰，辯者馳說，智者應機，謀夫演略，武士奮威，雲合霧集，風激電飛，量時揆宜，用取世資，小屈大申，存公忽私，雖尺枉而尋直，終揚光以發輝也。

translations.literal: Therefore the penetrating man studies the Way, probes the deep and seeks the subtle, observes heaven's movement's tally-signs, examines human affairs' flourishing and decline; debaters gallop persuasions, wise men respond to opportunity, planners unfold stratagems, martial knights rouse awe; cloud joins mist gathers, wind lashes lightning flies; measure the time assess the fit, use to take age's resources; small bend great stretch, preserve public neglect private; although a foot bent yet a fathom straight—in the end raise light to emit radiance.
translations.idiomatic: The adept probes principle, reads heaven’s signs and human fortune, while debaters, strategists, and warriors surge like storm clouds; they seize the moment, bend a little to win much, set the public good above private ease—a short crook may yield a long straight, and their light shines forth at last.

sentences.zh: 今三方鼎跱，九有未乂，悠悠四海，嬰丁禍敗，嗟道義之沉塞，愍生民之顛沛，此誠聖賢拯救之秋，烈士樹功之會也。

translations.literal: Now three sides tripod-stand, nine regions not yet governed; long long four seas, people meet calamity and defeat; sigh the Way and righteousness's sunken blockage, pity the living people's overturning—this truly is sage worthies' rescue season, ardent knights' establish-merit's meeting.
translations.idiomatic: The three powers stand like a tripod, the nine domains are still unsettled, and the people are caught in ruin; with the Way blocked and folk in misery, this is the very hour for sages to save the age and for heroes to win their fame.

sentences.zh: 吾子以高朗之才，珪璋之質，兼覽博窺，留心道術，無遠不致，無幽不悉；

translations.literal: You sir by lofty bright talent, scepter-jade's substance, concurrently viewing broad peering, fixing mind on Way and technique—nothing far not reached, nothing hidden not fully known;
translations.idiomatic: You have a brilliant mind and jade-like gifts, read widely, and master every branch of learning, high or low;

sentences.zh: 挺身取命，幹茲奧秘，躊躇紫闥，喉舌是執，九考不移，有入無出，

translations.literal: Stood body to take command, stem this deep secret; linger purple doors; throat and tongue is grasped; nine examinations not moved; there is entering without exiting,
translations.idiomatic: you stepped forward to take office, mastered its deepest workings, lingered at the purple portals as voice of the court, passed review after review without wavering, and have entered the inner circle without stepping back out—

sentences.zh: 〈《尚書》曰：三載考績，三考黜陟幽明。

translations.literal: 〈The Documents states: Every three years examine merit; three examinations demote and promote the dim and bright.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says that merit was reviewed every three years and that three such rounds decided promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 九考則二十七年。〉

translations.literal: Nine examinations then twenty-seven years.〉
translations.idiomatic: Nine rounds of review mean twenty-seven years.〉

sentences.zh: 究古今之真偽，計時務得失。

translations.literal: Exhaust ancient and modern's true and false; reckon current affairs' gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: You weigh truth and falsehood across the ages and judge the gains and losses of the present hour.

sentences.zh: 雖時獻一策，偶進一言，釋彼官責，慰此素餐，固未能輸竭忠款，盡瀝胸肝，排方入直，惠彼黎元，俾吾徒草鄙並有聞焉也。

translations.literal: Although sometimes offer one plan, occasionally advance one word, release that office's blame, console this white-rice eating—solidly was unable to pour out exhaust loyal sincerity, exhaust strain chest and liver, push aside square enter straight, benefit those black-haired people, cause our sort grass-low together to have fame therein.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you only offer a plan now and then or a word when chance allows, enough to meet your office and quiet a guilty conscience, you have hardly poured out your whole loyalty, laid bare your heart, cleared every obstacle for the straight path, or blessed the common people so that humble folk like us might share your renown.

sentences.zh: 盍亦綏衡綏轡，回軌易塗，輿安駕肆，思馬斯徂，審歷揭以投濟，要夷庚之赫憮，播秋蘭以芳世，副吾徒之彼圖，不亦盛與！

translations.literal: Why not also ease crossbar ease bridle, turn track change path, carriage safe drive at ease, horses think thus go; examine wade deep and shallow to cast to ford; seek smooth highway's bright shine; spread autumn orchid to fragrance the age; match our companions' that plan—is it not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Why not slacken the reins, change course, ride in comfort and let your horses turn homeward, ford only where the depth is sure, aim for the open high road, sow your virtue like autumn orchids through the world, and answer our hopes in grand style—is that not a finer thing!

sentences.zh: 』余聞而歎曰：『嗚呼，有若雲乎邪！

translations.literal: I heard and sighed saying: Alas, is it like clouds!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, I sighed: Alas—how insubstantial as a cloud!

sentences.zh: 夫人心不同，實若其面，子雖光麗，既美且艷，管窺筐舉，守厥所見，未可以言八紘之形埒，信萬事之精練也。

translations.literal: Now men's hearts are not the same, truly like their faces; you although bright beautiful, already fine yet splendid—tube peering basket lifting, guarding that which you see—not can thereby speak of eight cords' form and border, trust ten thousand affairs' refined mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts differ as faces do; bright as your speech is, it is still peering through a tube or scooping with a basket—clinging to one narrow view hardly maps the whole realm or proves mastery of every affair.

sentences.zh: 』或人率爾，仰而揚衡曰：『是何言與！

translations.literal: Someone rashly, looked up and raised the brow-ridge saying: What sort of words is this!
translations.idiomatic: The man flushed, threw back his head, and cried: What talk is this!

sentences.zh: 是何言與！』」

translations.literal: What sort of words is this!'"
translations.idiomatic: What talk is this!'"

sentences.zh: 余應之曰：「虞帝以面從為戒，孔聖以悅己為尤。

translations.literal: I answered him saying: 'The Yu Emperor took face-following as a warning; the Kong sage took pleasing oneself as fault.'
translations.idiomatic: I replied: Shun warned against flattering agreement, and Confucius counted self-pleasing a grave fault.

sentences.zh: 若子之言，良我所思，將為吾子論而釋之。

translations.literal: As for your words, truly what I ponder—I will for you sir discourse and explain.
translations.idiomatic: Your words are much on my mind; let me set out my answer for you.

sentences.zh: 昔在鴻荒，朦昧肇初，三皇應菉，五帝承符，爰暨夏、商，前典攸書。

translations.literal: Formerly in vast wildness, dim confusion began the first; Three Sovereigns responded to the green tally; Five Emperors received the token; then reaching Xia and Shang, former canons thereby wrote.
translations.idiomatic: In primordial chaos, before light broke, the Three Sovereigns answered heaven’s signs and the Five Emperors received the mandate; down through Xia and Shang the old texts record it.

sentences.zh: 姬衰道缺，霸者冀扶，嬴氏慘虐，吞嚼八區，於是從橫雲起，狙詐如星，奇衺蠭動，智故萌生；

translations.literal: Ji declined, the Way lacked; hegemons hoped to prop; the Ying clan cruelly ravaged, swallowed and chewed the eight regions—then vertical and horizontal rose like clouds, sniper deceit like stars, strange deviance swarmed like bees, clever schemes sprouted;
translations.idiomatic: When the house of Zhou waned and the Way faltered, hegemons strove to shore it up; the Qin tyrants devoured the realm, alliance and defiance swirled like clouds, treachery glittered like stars, perverse schemes swarmed, and cunning multiplied;

sentences.zh: 或飾真以仇偽，或挾邪以干榮，或詭道以要上，或鬻技以自矜；

translations.literal: some adorned truth to hate the false, some clasped deviance to seek glory, some twisted the Way to importune superiors, some sold skills to boast themselves;
translations.idiomatic: some masked truth to attack pretense, some peddled vice for favor, some used crooked means to sway their lords, some hawked tricks to puff themselves up;

sentences.zh: 背正崇邪，棄直就佞，忠無定分，義無常經。

translations.literal: turned back on straight, honored deviance; abandoned straight, approached flattery; loyalty had no fixed allotment, righteousness had no constant norm.
translations.idiomatic: straight paths were spurned for crooked ones, loyalty lost its measure, and duty its steady rule.

sentences.zh: 故鞅法窮而慝作，斯義敗而姦成，呂門大而宗滅，韓辯立而身刑。

translations.literal: Therefore Shang Yang's laws ended and evil arose; Si's righteousness failed and treachery succeeded; Lu's gate was great yet the clan extinguished; Han's disputation stood yet the body punished.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Yang’s laws ran their course and wickedness flourished; Li Si’s “righteousness” collapsed into villainy; the Lü clan rose high and was wiped out; Han Fei won fame with his rhetoric yet died by the headsman’s blade.

sentences.zh: 夫何故哉？

translations.literal: Now what cause?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 利回其心，寵耀其目，赫赫龍章，鑠鑠車服。

translations.literal: Profit turned their hearts; favor dazzled their eyes; blazing dragon insignia, shining carriage and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Gain twisted their hearts, favor dazzled their eyes, and the glitter of rank and equipage blinded them.

sentences.zh: 偷幸苟得，如反如仄，淫邪荒迷，恣睢自極，和鸞未調而身在轅側，庭寧未踐而櫟折榱覆。

translations.literal: Stole luck and grasped gain, like reverse like slant; wanton deviance wild lost, wanton stare self-extreme; harmony bells not yet tuned yet body at axle-side; courtyard calm not yet trod yet rafter broke ridgepole overturned.
translations.idiomatic: They grasped at luck and ill-gotten gain, wallowed in license, and rushed to extremes—the carriage bells were not yet tuned when they lay crushed beside the axle; they never reached the quiet court before the roof beam snapped and the rafters fell.

sentences.zh: 天收其精，地縮其澤，人吊其躬，鬼芟其額。

translations.literal: Heaven gathered their essence; earth shrank their marshes; people mourned their bodies; ghosts mowed their foreheads.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven withdrew their spirit, earth withheld its bounty, men mourned their corpses, and spirits mowed them down.

sentences.zh: 初升高岡，終隕幽壑，朝含榮潤，夕為枯魄。

translations.literal: At first climbed high hill; in the end fell into dark ravine; morning held glory's moisture; evening became withered soul.
translations.idiomatic: They climbed high at dawn and fell into the pit by dusk—flush with honor in the morning, a dry husk by night.

sentences.zh: 是以賢人君子，深圖遠慮，畏彼咎戾，超然高舉，寧曳屬於塗中，穢濁世之休譽。

translations.literal: Therefore worthy men and gentlemen, deep plans far thought, feared that blame and fault; transcendentally high raised—rather drag tail in mud in the path, defile the age's fair praise.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the wise planned far ahead, dreaded such ruin, and rose above the world—rather drag their tails in the mire than chase the age’s hollow praise.

sentences.zh: 彼豈輕主慢民，而忽於時務哉？

translations.literal: Did they lightly lord and slight people, and neglect current affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Did they despise ruler and people or scorn the tasks of the hour?

sentences.zh: 蓋《易》著行止之戒，《詩》有靖恭之歎，乃神之聽之而道使之然也。

translations.literal: For the Changes sets forth walking-stopping's warning; the Odes has quiet-respect's sigh—it is the spirits hearing it and the Way making it thus.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes warns when to act and when to stop; the Odes sighs over quiet reverence—the spirits hear, and the Way ordains such restraint.

sentences.zh: 自我大漢，應天順民，政治之隆，皓若陽春，俯憲坤典，仰式乾文。

translations.literal: From our Great Han, responding to heaven and following the people, governance's height, bright as yang spring; bowing take as model earth's canon, looking up pattern heaven's pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Our mighty Han answered Heaven and served the people; its government shone like spring; it took earth’s pattern below and heaven’s pattern above.

sentences.zh: 播皇澤以熙世，揚茂化之酢醇，君臣覆度，各守厥真，上垂詢納之弘，下有匡救之責，士無虛華之寵，民有一行之跡，粲乎亹亹，尚此忠益。

translations.literal: Spread imperial moisture to brighten the age; raise lush transformation's rich brew; ruler and minister repeated measure, each guarded their truth; above hung consultation-reception's greatness; below had correction-rescue's duty; knights had no empty splendor's favor; people had one conduct's trace; splendidly diligent, esteemed this loyal benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial grace warmed the world and fine instruction spread; ruler and minister each kept their station—high policy welcomed counsel, officials bore duty to set things right; scholars shunned empty honors, commoners kept to plain conduct; all strove in loyal service.

sentences.zh: 然而道有隆窳，物有興廢，有聲有寂，有光有翳。

translations.literal: Yet the Way has rise and decay; things have rise and fall; there is sound and there is silence; there is light and there is shade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Way waxes and wanes, things rise and fall, sound yields to silence, and light to shadow.

sentences.zh: 朱陽否於素秋，玄陰抑於孟春，羲和逝而望舒系，運氣匿而耀靈陳。

translations.literal: Red yang blocked in plain autumn; black yin suppressed in first spring; Xi He departed yet Wang Shu tied; moving qi hid yet shining spirit displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The yang sun can wane in bright autumn, yin can lift in early spring; the charioteer of day gives way to the moon’s reins; fortune hides and the bright spirit shows itself in turn.

sentences.zh: 沖、質不永，桓、靈墜敗，英雄雲布，豪傑蓋世，家挾殊議，人懷異計。

translations.literal: Chong, Zhi not long-lasting; Huan, Ling fell defeated; heroes cloud spread, stalwarts cover the age; households clasped diverse opinions; people harbored different schemes.
translations.idiomatic: The child emperors died young; Huan and Ling brought ruin; heroes and champions filled the land, each household with its own doctrine and each man his own design.

sentences.zh: 故從橫者欻披其胸。

translations.literal: Therefore the vertical-horizontal ones suddenly split their breasts.
translations.idiomatic: Alliance-mongers laid bare their breasts in haste.

sentences.zh: 狙詐者暫吐其舌也。

translations.literal: The sniper deceivers briefly spat their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Deceivers flicked out their tongues for a moment.

sentences.zh: 今天綱已綴，德樹西鄰，丕顯祖之宏規，縻好爵於士人，興五教以訓俗，豐九德濟民，肅明祀以礿祭，幾皇道以輔真。

translations.literal: Now heaven's net already restrung, virtue planted by the western neighbor, greatly displaying the ancestors' grand plan, tying fine ranks to knights, raising the five teachings to train custom, enriching the nine virtues to aid the people, solemn bright sacrifice with spring offering, nearing the royal Way to assist truth.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s net is whole again, virtue rises from the western court, the grand design of the founding ancestors shines, fine titles bind the gentry, the five teachings instruct custom, the nine virtues enrich the people, sacrifices are ordered in the spring rite, and the royal Way draws near to uphold the true.

sentences.zh: 雖跱者未一，偽者未分，聖人垂戒，蓋均無貧；

translations.literal: Although the standing-tall are not yet one, the false not yet sorted—the sage's hanging warning: 'perhaps none poor';
translations.idiomatic: Though factions still stand apart and the false are not yet sifted out, the sage’s warning holds: share alike and none need be poor;

sentences.zh: 故君臣協美於朝，黎庶欣戴於野，動若重規，靜若疊矩。

translations.literal: Therefore ruler and minister harmonized beauty at court, common people joyfully submitted in the wilds; moving like doubled compass, still like stacked square.
translations.idiomatic: So ruler and minister work in harmony at court and the people gladly support them in the fields—motion like nested compasses, rest like stacked squares.

sentences.zh: 濟濟偉彥，元凱之倫也，有過必知，顏子之仁也．侃侃庶政，冉、季之治也，鷹揚鷙騰，伊、望之事也；

translations.literal: Crowding great talents, Yuan and Kai's sort; having fault surely knowing—Yanzi's benevolence; forthrightly forthright many affairs—Ran and Ji's governance; eagle-soar fierce-bird leap—Yi and Wang's tasks;
translations.idiomatic: The court teems with talents like the eight worthies of Yao’s age; faults are known at once, as with Yan Hui’s candor; government runs firm and clear as under Ran and Ji; hawklike vigor matches the deeds of Yi Yin and Lü Wang;

sentences.zh: 總羣俊之上略，含薛氏之三計，敷張、陳之秘策，故力徵以勤世，援化英而不遑，豈暇修枯籜於榛穢哉！

translations.literal: Gathered the host of excellence's upper strategy, contained the Xue clan's three plans, spread out Zhang and Chen's secret stratagems—therefore strove with force to toil the age, grasped transforming heroes without leisure—how leisure to trim withered bamboo-sheath in thorny filth!
translations.idiomatic: They marshal the best minds, hold Xue Gong’s three counsels, and deploy the secret designs of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping—so busy driving the age forward they have no time to fuss over dead husks in the brambles!

sentences.zh: 然吾不才，在朝累紀，托身所天，心焉是恃。

translations.literal: Yet I lack talent; at court many years; entrusted body to what heaven grants; heart thereby relies.
translations.idiomatic: I am untalented yet have served at court for years, my life lodged with my sovereign, my heart set on that alone.

sentences.zh: 樂滄海之廣深，歎篙岳之高跱，聞仲尼之贊商，感鄉校之益己，彼平仲之和羹，亦近可而替否；

translations.literal: Rejoiced in blue sea's breadth and depth; sighed at Song mountain's height standing; heard Zhongni's praise of Shang; felt village school's benefit to self; that Pingzhong's harmonizing broth—also near can yet replace no;
translations.idiomatic: I delight in the vast sea, marvel at Mount Song’s height, recall Confucius’s praise of the Shang, and feel how the village school helped me; like Yan Ying’s harmonizing stew, one may be near enough to judge what is fit and what is not;

sentences.zh: 故矇冒瞽說，時有攸獻，譬遒人之有採於市閭，遊童之吟詠乎疆畔，庶以增廣福祥，輸力規諫。

translations.literal: Therefore dimly risk blind speech, at times had what to offer—like the road-man's having gathering in market lanes, roaming children's chanting at field borders—hoping thereby to increase and widen blessing auspicious, convey strength in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: So I risk blind words at times, like a herald gathering songs in the lanes or children humming at the field’s edge—hoping to add some blessing and lend my feeble voice to remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 若其合也，則以暗協明，進應靈符；

translations.literal: If it fits, then by dark harmonize brightness, advance respond to spirit tally;
translations.idiomatic: If they fit the moment, my dim words may chime with bright policy and answer heaven’s signs;

sentences.zh: 如其違也，自我常分，退守己愚。

translations.literal: If they violate, from self constant allotment, withdraw and guard one's folly.
translations.idiomatic: if not, I fall back on my proper lot and keep my own foolish peace.

sentences.zh: 進退任數，不矯不誣，循性樂天，夫何恨諸？

translations.literal: Advance and retreat trust fate, not forced not false, follow nature rejoice in heaven—what hatred therein?
translations.idiomatic: I advance or withdraw as fate allows, neither forcing nor deceiving; following my nature and accepting Heaven—what is there to resent?

sentences.zh: 此其所既入不出，有而若無者也。

translations.literal: This is that whereby having entered yet not exiting, having yet seems as without.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by entering and not leaving—holding office yet seeming not to hold it.

sentences.zh: 狹屈氏之常醒，濁漁父之必醉，溷柳季之卑等辱，編夷、叔之高懟。

translations.literal: Deemed narrow the Qu clan's constant waking-sober; deemed turbid the fisherman's must-drunk; confused Liuxia Hui's low-rank shame; strung Boyi and Shuqi's high indignation.
translations.idiomatic: I reject Qu Yuan’s endless vigil and the fisherman’s counsel to drown care in wine; I do not confuse Liuxia Hui’s patient low station with Boyi and Shuqi’s lofty umbrage.

sentences.zh: 合不以得，違以不失，得不克詘，失不慘悸。

translations.literal: In accord not because of gain; in violation not because of loss; gain does not overcome bend; loss does not bitterly tremble.
translations.idiomatic: In success I do not cling to profit; in setback I do not cling to loss—gain cannot bend me, loss cannot terrify me.

sentences.zh: 不樂前以顧軒，不就後以慮輊，不鬻譽以乾澤，不辭愆以忌絀。

translations.literal: Not rejoice in front to look at high carriage-bar; not approach back to fear low carriage-tail; not sell fame to beg moisture; not decline fault to fear demotion.
translations.idiomatic: I do not preen over what lies ahead nor brood on what trails behind; I hawk no praise for favor and shun no fault from fear of demotion.

sentences.zh: 何責之釋？

translations.literal: What blame's release?
translations.idiomatic: What charge must I clear?

sentences.zh: 何餐之卹？

translations.literal: What meal's pity?
translations.idiomatic: What salary shames my conscience?

sentences.zh: 何方之排？

translations.literal: What square's push-aside?
translations.idiomatic: What crooked corner must I elbow aside?

sentences.zh: 何直之入？

translations.literal: What straight's enter?
translations.idiomatic: What straight gate must I force my way into?

sentences.zh: 九考不移，固其所執也。

translations.literal: Nine examinations not moved—solidly that which is grasped.
translations.idiomatic: Through nine rounds of review I have not wavered—that is the grip I keep.

sentences.zh: 方今朝士山積，髦俊成羣，猶鱗介之潛乎巨海，毛羽之集乎鄧林，游禽逝不為之鮮，浮魴臻不為之殷。

translations.literal: Just now court knights mountain-pile, fine talents form groups—like scales and shells hidden in the great sea, feathers and down gathered on Deng forest; roaming birds passing not for this few, floating bream arriving not for this many.
translations.idiomatic: The court teems with talent like shells in the deep sea or birds in the magic grove—one more arrival neither thins nor crowds the press.

sentences.zh: 且陽靈幽於唐葉，陰精應於商時，陽盱請而洪災息，桑林禱而甘澤滋。

translations.literal: Moreover yang spirit dimmed in Tang's reign; yin essence responded in Shang's time; Yangxu plea and great flood ceased; mulberry grove prayer and sweet moisture nourished.
translations.idiomatic: The bright sun once hid in Tang’s age and yin answered in Shang’s; Yu offered himself at the Yangxu River and the flood stilled; Tang prayed in the mulberry grove and sweet rain fell.

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：禹為水，以身請於陽盱之河，湯苦旱，以身禱於桑林之際，聖人之憂民，如此其明也。

translations.literal: 〈The Huainanzi states: Yu for the waters, with body pleaded at Yangxu River; Tang suffered drought, with body prayed at mulberry grove's border—the sages' care for the people was thus this clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says Yu threw himself on the waters at the Yangxu River and Tang prayed in person at the mulberry grove—so plainly did sages grieve for the people.

sentences.zh: 《呂氏春秋》曰：昔殷湯克夏桀而天下大旱，三年不收，湯乃以身禱於桑林曰：「余一人有罪，無及萬方，萬方有罪，在余一人，無以一人之不敏，使上帝毀傷民之大命。

translations.literal: The Lüshi chunqiu states: Formerly Yin Tang overcame Xia Jie yet the realm great drought, three years no harvest; Tang then with body prayed at mulberry grove saying: 'I alone have guilt—let it not reach the myriad regions; the myriad regions have guilt—it rests in me alone; do not because one man's dullness make High Lord destroy and wound the people's great mandate.'
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi chunqiu records that after Tang conquered Jie a three-year drought struck; Tang prayed at the mulberry grove: if guilt lies anywhere, let it be mine alone—do not let one dull ruler make Heaven harm the people’s life.

sentences.zh: 」湯於是剪其髮，攦其爪，自以為犧牲，用祈福於上帝。

translations.literal: " Tang thereupon cut his hair, plucked his nails, took himself as sacrificial victim, used to seek blessing from High Lord.
translations.idiomatic: He cut his hair and nails and offered himself as a victim to seek Heaven’s blessing.

sentences.zh: 民乃甚悅。

translations.literal: The people then greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced greatly.

sentences.zh: 雨乃大至。〉

translations.literal: Rain then greatly arrived.〉
translations.idiomatic: Then the rains came in torrents.〉

sentences.zh: 行止有道，啟塞有期。

translations.literal: Walking and stopping have a Way; opening and blocking have a season.
translations.idiomatic: Going and staying follow the Way; opening and closing have their season.

sentences.zh: 我師遺訓，不怨不尤，委命恭己，我又何辭？

translations.literal: Our master's handed teaching: no resentment no fault-finding; entrust fate, revere self—what more have I to say?
translations.idiomatic: Our teacher left us: blame no one, bow to fate, and cultivate the self—what answer need I add?

sentences.zh: 辭窮路單，將反初節，綜墳典之流勞，尋孔氏之遺藝，綴微辭以存道，儘先軌而投制，題叔肸之優遊，美疏氏之遐逝，收止足以言歸，泛皓然以容裔，欣環堵以恬娛，免咎悔於斯世，顧茲心之未泰，懼末塗之泥滯，仍求激而增憤，肆中懷以告誓。

translations.literal: Words exhausted road lone—about to return to first integrity; comb tomb canons' flowing toil, seek Kong clan's handed arts; stitch subtle phrases to preserve the Way, follow former tracks and cast to regulation; inscribe Shu's Xi ease-roaming, praise the Su clan's far going; gather stop-foot enough to speak return, float bright-wide to drift; rejoice ringed wall for quiet joy; avoid fault-regret in this age; look back at this heart's not peace; fear last path's mud-stuck; again seek sharp and increase indignation; unleash center breast to declare oath.
translations.idiomatic: My words are spent and the road bare; I will return to my first resolve, review the classics and Confucius’s arts, string modest lines to keep the Way, follow ancient models and accept restraint, praise Shu Xi’s ease and the Su elders’ withdrawal, know when enough is enough and turn homeward, drift in broad clarity, find quiet joy within humble walls, and escape blame in this world—yet my heart is not at ease, I fear sticking in the mud at the end, so I press on in sharper vexation and lay bare my breast in this vow.

sentences.zh: 昔九方考精於至貴，秦牙沈思於殊形；

translations.literal: Formerly Jiufang examined essence in utmost worth; Qin Ya sank thought in strange form;
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiufang Yan read the inner worth of horses and Qin Ya pondered their outward form;

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：秦穆公謂伯樂曰：「子之年長矣，子姓有可使求馬者乎？

translations.literal: 〈The Huainanzi states: Duke Mu of Qin said to Bole: 'Your years are long; among your sons and kin is there one who can be sent to seek horses?'
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says Duke Mu of Qin asked Bole: you are old; is there a son or kinsman who can find horses for me?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「良馬者，可以形容筋骨相也。

translations.literal: " He answered saying: 'A fine horse—one can by form appearance sinews bones inspect it.'
translations.idiomatic: Bole replied: a good horse can be judged from its build and bones.

sentences.zh: 相天下之馬者，若滅若沒，若失若亡，其一若此馬者，絕塵卻轍。

translations.literal: Inspecting the realm's horse—like vanish like sink, like lose like perish; if one like this horse, cuts dust casts back wheel-track.
translations.idiomatic: A horse of the finest breed seems to vanish and leave no clear outline; when one appears, it outruns the dust and erases its tracks.

sentences.zh: 臣之子皆下才也，可告以良馬而不可告以天下之馬。

translations.literal: Your subject's sons are all lower talent; can be told about fine horses but cannot be told about the realm's horse.
translations.idiomatic: My sons are mediocre: they can spot a good horse but not a horse of the realm’s finest kind.

sentences.zh: 天下之馬，臣有所與共儋纏採薪九方堙，此其相馬，非臣之下也，請見之。

translations.literal: As for the realm's horse, your subject has one who together with him carries loads and gathers firewood—Jiufang Yan—this one's inspecting horses is not below your subject; please see him.
translations.idiomatic: For that I have a woodcutter named Jiufang Yan who is my match as a judge of horses; let him attend you.

sentences.zh: 」穆公見之，使之求馬，三月而反，報曰：「已得馬矣，在於沙丘。

translations.literal: " Duke Mu saw him, sent him to seek horses; three months then returned, reported saying: 'Already obtained horse; it is at Shaqiu.'
translations.idiomatic: The duke received him and sent him off; three months later he reported: I have found the horse at Shaqiu.

sentences.zh: 」穆公曰：「何馬也？

translations.literal: " Duke Mu said: 'What horse?'
translations.idiomatic: What kind of horse?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「牝而黃。

translations.literal: " He answered saying: 'Female and yellow.'
translations.idiomatic: A yellow mare.

sentences.zh: 」使人往取之，牡而驪。

translations.literal: " Sent a man to go fetch it—it was male and black.
translations.idiomatic: Men fetched it: it was a black stallion.

sentences.zh: 穆公不悅，召伯樂而問之曰：「敗矣，子之所使求馬者也！

translations.literal: Duke Mu was not pleased; summoned Bole and asked him saying: 'Ruined—he whom you sent to seek horses!'
translations.idiomatic: The duke was displeased and summoned Bole: your agent has ruined the search!

sentences.zh: 毛物牝牡尚弗能知，又何馬之能知？

translations.literal: Hair thing female male still not able to know—what then horse able to know?
translations.idiomatic: He cannot even tell a mare from a stallion or the coat—how can he know a true steed?

sentences.zh: 」伯樂喟然太息曰：「一至此乎！

translations.literal: " Bole sighed greatly and said: 'Has it reached this!'
translations.idiomatic: Bole sighed: has it come to this!

sentences.zh: 是乃所以千萬

translations.literal: This is that whereby he surpasses a thousand myriads
translations.idiomatic: That is why he outranks

translations.literal: (li [interlinear note])
translations.idiomatic: countless

sentences.zh: 臣而無數者也。

translations.literal: of servants like your subject—without reckoning of their number.
translations.idiomatic: ordinary agents like me put together.

sentences.zh: 若堙之所觀者天機也，得其精而忘其粗，在其內而忘其外，見其所見而不見其所不見，視其所視而遺其所不視，若彼之所相者，乃有貴乎馬者。

translations.literal: As for what Yan observes—it is heaven's pivot; obtaining its essence and forgetting its coarse, being in its inner and forgetting its outer; seeing what he sees and not seeing what he does not see; viewing what he views and losing what he does not view—as for that which he inspects, then there is something more precious than horse.
translations.idiomatic: What Yan sees is the heavenly spark: he grasps the spirit and forgets the hide, the inward and not the outward—what he notices he notices, what he ignores he ignores; what he judges is more precious than any mere horse.

sentences.zh: 」馬至，而果天下之馬也。

translations.literal: " When the horse arrived, it indeed was the realm's horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the horse arrived, it proved indeed a steed of the realm’s finest kind.

sentences.zh: 淮南子又曰：伯樂、寒風、秦牙、葛青，所相各異，其知馬一也；

translations.literal: Huainanzi again states: Bole, Hanfeng, Qin Ya, Ge Qing—what each inspected differed; their knowing horses was one;
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi adds that Bole, Hanfeng, Qin Ya, and Ge Qing each judged horses differently yet understood horses in the same way;

sentences.zh: 蓋九方觀其精，秦牙察其形。〉

translations.literal: For Jiufang observed its essence, Qin Ya inspected its form.〉
translations.idiomatic: Jiufang read the spirit, Qin Ya the outward form.〉

sentences.zh: 薛燭察寶以飛譽，

translations.literal: Xue Zhu inspected treasure thereby flying fame,
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhu appraised a treasure and won sudden fame;

sentences.zh: 〈《越絕書》曰：昔越王句踐有寶劍五枚，聞於天下。

translations.literal: 〈The Yue jue shu states: Formerly King Goujian of Yue had precious swords five pieces, famed in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Yue jue shu says King Goujian of Yue once owned five famous swords.

sentences.zh: 客有能相劍者名薛燭，王召而問之：「吾有寶劍五，請以示子。

translations.literal: A guest able to inspect swords named Xue Zhu; the king summoned and asked him: 'I have precious swords five—please to show you.'
translations.idiomatic: A guest named Xue Zhu could judge swords; the king summoned him: I have five treasure blades—let me show them.

sentences.zh: 」乃取豪曹、臣闕，薛燭曰：「皆非也。

translations.literal: " Then took Haocao, Juque; Xue Zhu said: 'Neither is it.'
translations.idiomatic: He brought out Haocao and Juque; Xue Zhu said: neither is the one.

sentences.zh: 」又取純鉤、湛盧，燭曰：「觀其劍鈔，爛爛如列宿之行，觀其光，渾渾如水之將溢於塘，觀其文，渙渙如冰將釋，此所謂純鉤邪？

translations.literal: " Again took Chungou, Zhanlu; Zhu said: 'Observe its sword's edge—brilliant as ranked stars' motion; observe its light—rolling as water about to overflow the pond; observe its pattern—dissolving as ice about to melt—this is what is called Chungou?'
translations.idiomatic: He produced Chungou and Zhanlu; Zhu said: see how the edge glitters like constellations in motion, how the gleam swells like water brimming a pool, how the grain flows like melting ice—is this Chungou?

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「是也。

translations.literal: " The king said: 'It is so.'
translations.idiomatic: The king said: yes.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「客有直之者，有市之鄉三，駿馬千匹，千戶之都二，可乎？

translations.literal: " The king said: 'If someone wished to purchase it—three market towns, a thousand swift horses, two thousand-household capitals—would it do?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked: if someone offered three trading towns, a thousand horses, and two cities of a thousand households—would that buy it?

sentences.zh: 」薛燭曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " Xue Zhu said: 'Not possible.'
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhu said: not for any price.

sentences.zh: 當造此劍之時，赤堇之山破而出錫，若邪之谿涸而出銅，雨師掃灑，雷公擊鼓，太一下觀，天精下之，歐冶乃因天之精，悉其伎巧，一曰純鉤，二曰湛盧。

translations.literal: When this sword was forged, Chijing mountain split and yielded tin; Ruoye's stream dried and yielded copper; rain master swept; thunder duke beat drums; Grand One descended to look; heaven's essence descended; Ou Yezi then by heaven's essence, exhausted his skill and craft—first called Chungou, second called Zhanlu.
translations.idiomatic: When it was forged, Mount Chijing split to yield tin and the Ruoye stream ran dry to yield copper; spirits swept the way and thunder rolled while the Grand One looked on and heaven’s essence descended; Ou Yezi used that power to exhaust his art—thus Chungou and Zhanlu.

sentences.zh: 今赤堇之山已合，若邪之谿深而不測，歐冶子已死，雖傾城量金，珠玉竭河，獨不得此一物。

translations.literal: Now Chijing mountain has closed; Ruoye's stream is deep and unfathomable; Ou Yezi is already dead—though overturn cities measure gold, pearls and jade exhaust the river, alone cannot obtain this one thing.
translations.idiomatic: Now the mountain has closed again, the stream runs too deep to fathom, and Ou Yezi is dead—though you razed cities and weighed out gold and emptied the river of pearls and jade, you could not win this blade alone.

sentences.zh: 有市之鄉三，駿馬千匹，千戶之都二，亦何足言與！」〉

translations.literal: Three market towns, a thousand swift horses, two thousand-household capitals—what worth speaking of!'"〉
translations.idiomatic: What are three towns, a thousand horses, or two cities compared with that!'"〉

sentences.zh: 瓠梁托弦以流聲；

translations.literal: Hu Liang entrusted strings thereby flowing sound;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Liang drew sound from his strings;

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：瓠巴鼓瑟而鱘魚聽之。

translations.literal: 〈The Huainanzi states: Hu Ba strummed the se and sturgeon fish listened.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says that when Hu Ba played the se, the fish rose to listen.

sentences.zh: 又曰：瓠梁之歌可隨也，而以歌者不可為也。〉

translations.literal: Again states: Hu Liang's song can be followed, yet to be the singer who does it cannot be matched.〉
translations.idiomatic: It also says one may follow Hu Liang’s songs, but no one can sing as he did.〉

sentences.zh: 齊隸拊髀以濟文，

translations.literal: A Qi groom slapped thigh thereby aiding Wen,
translations.idiomatic: a Qi groom slapped his thighs to save Lord Mengchang;

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之曰：按此謂孟嘗君田文下坐客，能作雞鳴以濟其厄者也。

translations.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi states: Examining this refers to Lord Mengchang Tian Wen's lower-seat guest, able to make cock-crow to aid his peril.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes this is the low-born guest of Lord Mengchang who crowed like a cock to save him from peril.

sentences.zh: 凡作雞鳴，必先拊髀，以傚雞之拊翼也。〉

translations.literal: Whenever making cock-crow, must first slap thigh, to imitate cock's slapping wings.〉
translations.idiomatic: To crow like a cock one first slaps the thigh, mimicking the bird’s wing-beats.〉

sentences.zh: 楚客潛寇以保荊：

translations.literal: A Chu guest secretly stole enemy thereby protecting Jing:
translations.idiomatic: a Chu retainer stole among the foe to save the state:

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：楚將子發好求技道之士。

translations.literal: 〈The Huainanzi states: Chu general Zifa loved to seek men of skill and Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says General Zifa of Chu loved to recruit men of odd skills.

sentences.zh: 楚有善為偷者，往見曰：「聞君求技道之士，臣偷也，原以技備一卒。

translations.literal: Chu had one good at being a thief; went to see saying: 'Heard you seek men of skill and Way—your subject is a thief; wishes by skill to fill one soldier.'
translations.idiomatic: A skilled thief came to him: you seek men of art—I am a thief; let me serve as one of your men.

sentences.zh: 」子發聞之，衣不及帶，冠不暇正，出見而禮之。

translations.literal: " Zifa heard it; clothes not reaching belt, cap not leisure to straighten—went out to see and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Zifa, hearing this, rushed out half-dressed and crooked-capped to receive him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰：「偷者，天下之盜也，何為禮之？

translations.literal: Attendants remonstrated saying: 'A thief is the realm's robber—why honor him?'
translations.idiomatic: His attendants protested: a thief is the worst of rogues—why honor him?

sentences.zh: 」君曰：「此非左右之所得與。

translations.literal: " The lord said: 'This is not what attendants may join in.'
translations.idiomatic: The lord said: that is not for you to decide.

sentences.zh: 」後無幾何，齊興兵伐楚。

translations.literal: " After not long, Qi raised troops to attack Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qi attacked Chu.

sentences.zh: 子發將師以當之，兵三卻。

translations.literal: Zifa led hosts to oppose them; the army thrice withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zifa led the army against them but was driven back three times.

sentences.zh: 楚賢大夫皆盡其計而悉其誠，齊師愈強。

translations.literal: Chu's worthy great officers all exhausted their plans and fully their sincerity—yet Qi host grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Chu’s wise ministers gave every plan and every ounce of zeal, yet Qi’s host grew stronger still.
