sentences.zh: 於是卒偷進請曰：「臣有薄技，原為君行之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldier-thief advanced and requested saying: 'Your subject has a slight skill; wishes to perform it for the lord.'
translations.idiomatic: Then the thief stepped forward: I have a small skill—let me use it for you.

sentences.zh: 」君曰「諾」。

translations.literal: " The lord said 'Yes.'"
translations.idiomatic: The lord said: very well."

sentences.zh: 偷即夜出，解齊將軍之帳，而獻之子發。

translations.literal: The thief then at night went out, undid Qi general's tent, and presented it to Zifa.
translations.idiomatic: That night the thief slipped into the camp, took down the Qi general’s tent, and brought it to Zifa.

sentences.zh: 子發使人歸之，曰：「卒有出採薪者，得將軍之帳，使使歸於執事。

translations.literal: Zifa sent men to return it, saying: 'A soldier who went out gathering firewood obtained the general's tent; envoys send it back to the steward.'
translations.idiomatic: Zifa sent it back with word that a foraging soldier had found the general’s tent and was returning it to his staff.

sentences.zh: 」明日又復往取枕，子發又使歸之。

translations.literal: " Next day again went to take pillow; Zifa again sent to return it.
translations.idiomatic: The next night he took the pillow; Zifa returned that too.

sentences.zh: 明日又復往取簪，子發又使歸之。

translations.literal: Next day again went to take hairpin; Zifa again sent to return it.
translations.idiomatic: The night after he took the hairpin, and again Zifa sent it back.

sentences.zh: 齊師聞之大駭，將軍與軍吏謀曰：「今日不去，楚軍恐取吾頭矣！

translations.literal: Qi army heard it and greatly feared; general and army clerks plotted saying: 'If today we do not leave, Chu army fears it will take our heads!'
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army was terrified; the general and his officers said: if we do not withdraw today, Chu will have our heads tomorrow!'

sentences.zh: 」即旋師而去。〉

translations.literal: " At once turned the army and departed.〉
translations.idiomatic: They broke camp and fled at once.〉

sentences.zh: 雍門援琴而挾說，

translations.literal: Yongmen took qin and carried persuasion,
translations.idiomatic: Yongmen Zhou took up his zither and pressed his argument;

sentences.zh: 〈桓譚《新論》曰：雍門周以琴見，孟嘗君曰：「先生鼓琴，亦能令文悲乎？

translations.literal: 〈Huan Tan's New Discourses states: Yongmen Zhou by qin had audience; Lord Mengchang said: 'Master, if you strum the qin, can you also make Wen sorrowful?'
translations.idiomatic: Huan Tan’s New Discourses tells how Yongmen Zhou played for Lord Mengchang, who asked whether he could move him to grief.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣之所能令悲者，先貴而後賤，昔富而今貧，擯壓窮巷，不交四鄰；

translations.literal: " He answered saying: 'What your servant can make sorrowful: first noble then base, once rich now poor, pressed aside in poor lane, not mingling with four neighbors;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou replied: I can move those who were high and are brought low, once rich and now poor, shut in a slum, shunned by neighbors;

sentences.zh: 不若身材高妙，懷質抱真，逢讒罹謗，怨結而不得信；

translations.literal: or not as body stature high and subtle, cherishing substance embracing truth, meeting slander suffering calumny, resentment knotted yet unable to be believed;
translations.idiomatic: or the man of fine presence and true heart who meets slander, is distrusted, and nurses a knot of wrong;

sentences.zh: 不若交歡而結愛，無怨而生離，遠赴絕國，無相見期；

translations.literal: or not as exchanged joy and knotted love, without resentment yet born separation, far gone to cut-off state, no meeting time;
translations.idiomatic: or lovers parted though blameless, banished to distant lands with no hope of meeting;

sentences.zh: 不若幼無父母，壯無妻兒，出以野澤為鄰，入用堀穴為家，困於朝夕，無所假貸：若此人者，但聞飛烏之號，秋風鳴條，則傷心矣，臣一為之援琴而長太息，未有不淒惻而涕泣者也。

translations.literal: Or not as young without father mother, mature without wife children; out take wild marsh as neighbor, in use dug hole as home; pressed by morning evening, nowhere to borrow: such a person—only hearing flying crow's cry, autumn wind sounding branches, then is wounded in heart; your servant once for him took qin and long great sigh—never not mournful-side and tear-weeping ones.
translations.idiomatic: Or the childless orphan who dwells in the wilds and a burrow, pressed day and night with nowhere to turn—for such a one the cry of a bird or wind in the trees is grief enough; one touch of my zither and a long sigh, and none fail to weep.

sentences.zh: 今若足下，居則廣廈高堂，連闥洞房，下羅帷，來清風；

translations.literal: Now as for you sir, dwelling then broad house high hall, linked doors deep chambers, lower gauze curtains, come clear breeze;
translations.idiomatic: But you live in mansions and deep chambers hung with gauze, cooled by clear breezes;

sentences.zh: 倡優在前，諂諛侍側，揚激楚，舞鄭妾，流聲以娛耳，練色以淫目；

translations.literal: Singers and jesters in front, flatterers wait at side; raise Ji Chu, dance Zheng concubines; flowing sound to please ear, refined colors to dazzle eye;
translations.idiomatic: singers and sycophants attend you, the air rings with Chu airs and Zheng dancers, sound and color feast ear and eye;

sentences.zh: 水戲則舫龍舟，建羽旗，鼓釣乎不測之淵；

translations.literal: Water play then barge dragon boat, raise feather flags, drum and fish in unfathomable's abyss;
translations.idiomatic: on the water you race dragon boats with feathered banners and angle the deep pools;

sentences.zh: 野遊則登平原，馳廣囿，強弩下高鳥，勇士格猛獸；

translations.literal: Wild excursion then climb open plain, gallop broad park, strong crossbow bring down high birds, brave knights grapple fierce beasts;
translations.idiomatic: in the field you gallop the open park, strike birds from the sky with strong crossbows, and pit brave men against beasts;

sentences.zh: 置酒娛樂，沈醉忘歸：方此之時，視天地曾不若一指，雖有善鼓琴，未能足下也。

translations.literal: Set wine pleasure music, sink drunk forget return: at this moment, view heaven and earth once not like one finger; although there is one good at strumming qin, cannot match you sir.
translations.idiomatic: wine and revelry leave you drunk past homecoming—then heaven and earth seem no bigger than a finger, and no player, however skilled, could move you as I might.

sentences.zh: 」孟嘗君曰：「固然！

translations.literal: " Lord Mengchang said: 'Indeed so!'
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang said: true enough.

sentences.zh: 」雍門周曰：「然臣竊為足下有所常悲。

translations.literal: " Yongmen Zhou said: 'Yet your servant privately for you sir has something constantly sorrowful.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said: yet I have long grieved for you in one respect.

sentences.zh: 夫角帝而困秦者君也，連五國而伐楚者又君也。

translations.literal: Now he who matched emperor and trapped Qin was you sir; linked five states and attacked Chu's was again you sir.
translations.idiomatic: You rivaled the emperors and penned Qin; you linked five states and struck Chu.

sentences.zh: 天下未嘗無事，不從即衡；

translations.literal: The realm never was without affairs—if not vertical alliance then horizontal;
translations.idiomatic: The realm is never still: without alliance there is defiance;

sentences.zh: 從成則楚王，衡成則秦帝。

translations.literal: Vertical alliance complete then Chu king; horizontal complete then Qin emperor.
translations.idiomatic: alliance makes Chu king; defiance crowns Qin emperor.

sentences.zh: 夫以秦、楚之強而報弱薛，猶磨蕭斧而伐朝菌也，有識之士，莫不為足下寒心。

translations.literal: Now with Qin and Chu's strength and repaying weak Xue—like grinding Xiao axe to cut morning fungus; knowing men, none not for you sir chill heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin or Chu turns on feeble Xue, it is like whetting an ax on a morning mushroom—every thoughtful man shudders for you.

sentences.zh: 天道不常盛，寒暑更進退，千秋萬歲之後，宗廟必不血食；

translations.literal: Heaven's Way is not constant flourishing; cold and heat alternate advance and retreat; after thousand autumns ten thousand years, ancestral temple surely will not blood-sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s way turns: cold and heat alternate; ages hence your line may no longer receive sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 高台既已傾，曲池又已平，墳墓生荊棘，狐狸穴其中，遊兒牧豎躑躅其足而歌其上曰：『孟嘗君之尊貴，亦猶若是乎！

translations.literal: High terrace already overturned, winding pool again leveled; tombs grow thorns and brambles, foxes burrow within; roaming boys shepherd lads pace their feet and sing atop saying: 'Lord Mengchang's honor and nobility—is it also thus!'
translations.idiomatic: your high towers will fall and your pools fill in; brambles will choke the tombs and foxes lair there while herd boys tramp the ruins singing: was Lord Mengchang’s glory any different from this!'

sentences.zh: 』」於是孟嘗君喟然太息，涕淚承睫而未下。

translations.literal: '" Thereupon Lord Mengchang sighed greatly, tears and weeping caught on lashes yet not falling.
translations.idiomatic: Mengchang gave a great sigh; tears welled in his eyes but did not fall.

sentences.zh: 雍門周引琴而鼓之，徐動宮徵，叩角羽，終而成曲，孟嘗君遂歔欷而就之曰：「先生鼓琴，令文立若亡國之人也。」〉

translations.literal: Yongmen Zhou drew qin and strummed it; slowly moved gong and zhi, struck jue and yu; in the end completed a tune; Lord Mengchang then sob-sniffed and drew near saying: 'Master strums qin—makes Wen stand as if a lost-state's person.'"〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhou drew a slow melody across the modes until a full tune formed; Mengchang drew near weeping: your playing leaves me standing like a man of a fallen state.'"〉

sentences.zh: 韓哀秉轡而馳名；

translations.literal: Han Ai grasped reins and galloped fame;
translations.idiomatic: Han Ai took the reins and won renown;

sentences.zh: 〈《呂氏春秋》曰：韓哀作禦。

translations.literal: 〈The Lüshi chunqiu states: Han Ai made charioteering.
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi chunqiu credits Han Ai with inventing the charioteer’s art.

sentences.zh: 王褒聖主得賢臣頌曰：及至駕齧膝，參乘旦，王良執靶，韓哀附輿，縱馳騁騖，忽如景靡，過都越國，蹶如歷塊，追奔電，逐遺風，周流八極，萬里一息，何其遼哉！

translations.literal: Wang Bao's Praise of the Sage Lord Obtaining Worthy Ministers states: Reaching to when driving knee-nibbler, three-rider dawn, Wang Liang grasped cheek-strap, Han Ai attached to carriage—let loose gallop and race, sudden as shadow's fall; pass capital cross state, stumble as treading clod; pursue running lightning, chase trailing wind; circulate eight poles, ten thousand li one breath—how vast!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao’s hymn tells of pairing knee-nipping steeds with Wang Liang on the reins and Han Ai at the carriage—horses that flash like shadows, leap capitals in a stride, outrun lightning and wind, circle the eight extremes and breathe once in ten thousand li—how vast that span!

sentences.zh: 人馬相得也。〉

translations.literal: Man and horse matched each other.〉
translations.idiomatic: Horse and rider were perfectly matched.〉

sentences.zh: 盧敖翱翔乎玄闕，若士竦身於雲清。

translations.literal: Lu Ao soared at Dark Gate; the Gentleman straightened body in cloud's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ao soared to the Dark Gate while the recluse rose into the clear clouds;

sentences.zh: 〈《淮南子》曰：盧敖遊乎北海，經乎太陰，入乎玄闕，至於蒙轂之上，見一士焉，深目而玄準，戾頸而鳶肩，豐上而殺下，軒軒然方迎風而舞，顧見盧敖慢然下其臂，遯逃乎碑下。

translations.literal: 〈The Huainanzi states: Lu Ao roamed at North Sea, passed through Great Yin, entered Dark Gate, reached upon Menggu's heights, saw a gentleman there: deep eyes and dark nose, twisted neck and kite shoulder, full above and tapering below, lofty lofty just facing wind and dancing; looking back saw Lu Ao, leisurely lowered his arms, fled to crouch beneath a stone.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says Lu Ao roamed the northern dark, entered the Black Gate, and on Mount Menggu met a strange man—deep-set eyes, hooked nose, kite shoulders, narrow hips—who danced in the wind, then spied Ao, dropped his arms, and slipped behind a stone.

sentences.zh: 盧敖俯而視之，方卷龜殼而食合梨。

translations.literal: Lu Ao bent and looked at him—just then rolling tortoise shell and eating helian pear.
translations.idiomatic: Ao bent close and saw him curled in a turtle shell, eating a pear.

sentences.zh: 盧敖乃與之語曰：「惟敖為背羣離黨，窮觀於六合之外者，非敖而已乎！

translations.literal: Lu Ao then spoke with him saying: 'Only Ao is one who turned back from the flock left the party, exhausted viewing beyond the six directions' outside—is it not Ao alone!'
translations.idiomatic: Ao said: I left the crowd to roam beyond the six directions—surely none but I have done that!'

sentences.zh: 敖幼而好遊，長不喻解，周行四極，惟北陰之不闚，今卒睹夫子於是，子殆可與敖為交乎！

translations.literal: Ao in youth loved roaming; grown not explained understanding; circled walked four poles; only north yin's not glimpsed; now suddenly see the master here—you perhaps can with Ao be friends!'
translations.idiomatic: I have wandered since boyhood to the four limits but never pierced the northern gloom; to meet you here—may we be companions!'

sentences.zh: 」若士者蠤然而笑曰：「嘻乎！

translations.literal: " The Gentleman then smiled thinly and said: 'Ha!'
translations.idiomatic: The man gave a thin smile: ha!

sentences.zh: 子中州民，寧肯而遠至此？

translations.literal: You central-region commoner—how could you willingly come this far?
translations.idiomatic: You are a man of the central plain—what brings you this far?

sentences.zh: 此猶光乎日月而戴列星，陰陽之所行，四時之所生，此其比夫不名之地，猶突奧也。

translations.literal: This still shines with sun and moon and bears ranked stars; yin and yang's moving; four seasons' birthing—this its compared to unnamed land is still like stove's corner.
translations.idiomatic: Here you stand bathed in sun and moon and the march of the seasons—set beside the nameless regions this is still a kitchen corner.

sentences.zh: 若我南游乎罔{罒良}之野，北息於沈墨之鄉，西窮冥冥之黨，東貫鴻濛之光，此其下無地而上無天，聽焉無聞，視焉則眴，此其外猶有沈沈之汜，其餘一舉而千萬里，吾猶未能之在。

translations.literal: As for me south roamed at Wangliang wilds (graph wang plus liang), north rested at Sinking-Ink's village, west exhausted dark-dark's clique, east pierced Vast-Mist's light—here below no earth and above no heaven; listening thereto no hearing, looking thereto then dizzy; beyond this still has deep-deep's ford; the rest one lift and thousand myriads of li—I still have not been able to reach there.
translations.idiomatic: I have roamed south to Wangliang’s wastes, north to the land of ink-black dusk, west to utter dark, east through primordial gleam—where there is neither earth below nor sky above, where sound dies and sight reels—beyond that lie depths I have not reached in a single leap of a million li.

sentences.zh: 今子遊始至於此，乃語窮觀，豈不亦遠哉！

translations.literal: Now you roam first reaching here, then speak of exhausted viewing—is it not also far!
translations.idiomatic: You have only just arrived and call it the ends of sight—is that not presumptuous!

sentences.zh: 然子處矣，吾與汗漫期於九垓之上，吾不可以久。

translations.literal: Yet you stay; I with Vast Wanderer have tryst on nine heights' above—I cannot long remain.
translations.idiomatic: Stay if you will; I have a tryst with Hanman beyond the nine heavens and cannot linger.

sentences.zh: 」若士舉臂而竦身，遂入雲中。

translations.literal: " The Gentleman raised arms and straightened body, then entered amid clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his arms, sprang up, and vanished into the clouds.

sentences.zh: 盧敖仰而視之，弗見乃止，曰：「吾比夫子也，猶黃鵠之與壤蟲，終日行不離咫尺，自以為遠，不亦悲哉！」〉

translations.literal: Lu Ao looked up and gazed; not seeing then stopped, saying: 'I compared to the master—like yellow swan's to soil worm; whole day walk not leave foot and inch; self thinking far—is it not sorrowful!'"〉
translations.idiomatic: Ao stared upward until he lost sight, then sighed: beside him I am a mayfly to a swan—I walked all day within inches and thought myself far—how pitiful!'"〉

sentences.zh: 余實不能齊技於數子，故乃靜然守己而自寧。」

translations.literal: I truly cannot equal skills with these several men—therefore then quietly guard self and self find peace.
translations.idiomatic: I truly cannot match those men in craft, so I keep still and find peace in myself.

sentences.zh: 景耀六年，後主從譙周之計，遣使請降於鄧艾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingyao, the Later Lord followed Qiao Zhou's plan, sent envoy to beg surrender from Deng Ai.
translations.idiomatic: In 263 the Later Lord followed Qiao Zhou’s counsel and sent envoys to surrender to Deng Ai.

sentences.zh: 其書，正所造也。

translations.literal: That letter—Zheng was the one who composed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng had drafted that letter.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，鐘會作亂成都，後主東遷洛陽，時擾攘倉卒。

translations.literal: Next year's first month, Zhong Hui made rebellion at Chengdu; Later Lord east moved to Luoyang; the time was tumultuous hasty.
translations.idiomatic: The next New Year Zhong Hui mutinied at Chengdu; the Later Lord was moved east to Luoyang in uproar and haste.

sentences.zh: 蜀之大臣無冀從者，惟正及殿中督汝南張通，捨妻子單身隨侍。

translations.literal: Shu's great ministers had none who hoped to follow; only Zheng and palace-inside supervisor Runan Zhang Tong, cast aside wife and children, alone body followed and attended.
translations.idiomatic: No Shu minister hoped to follow him except Zheng and the palace guard Zhang Tong of Runan, who left family and went alone in attendance.

sentences.zh: 後主賴正相導宜適，舉動無闕，乃慨然歎息，恨知正之晚，時論嘉之。

translations.literal: Later Lord relied on Zheng mutually guiding fitting and right; movements and acts without lack—then sighed greatly, regretted knowing Zheng late; contemporary discussion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord leaned on Zheng’s guidance in deportment and never misstepped; he sighed that he had known Zheng too late, and opinion praised Zheng.

sentences.zh: 賜爵關內候。

translations.literal: Granted rank Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，除安陽令，遷巴西太守。

translations.literal: In Taishi period, appointed Magistrate of Anyang, promoted Administrator of Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era he became magistrate of Anyang and then governor of Baxi.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年詔曰：「正昔在成都，顛沛守義，不違忠節，及見受用，盡心幹事，有治理之績，其以正為巴西太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taishi an edict said: 'Zheng formerly at Chengdu, in overturning preserved righteousness, did not violate loyal integrity; when received and employed, exhausted mind in managing affairs, had governance's traces—therefore make Zheng Administrator of Baxi.'
translations.idiomatic: In 272 an edict declared that in Chengdu’s turmoil Zheng had kept faith, and in office had governed well—so he was named governor of Baxi.

sentences.zh: 」咸寧四年卒。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year of Xianning died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 278.

sentences.zh: 凡所著述詩論賦之屬，垂百篇。

translations.literal: In all what he wrote and composed—poems, discourses, fu and the like—nearly one hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His poems, treatises, and fu numbered nearly a hundred.

sentences.zh: 評曰：杜微脩身隱靜，不役當世，庶幾夷、皓之槩。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Du Wei cultivated self, hidden and quiet, not serving the current age—perhaps nearly Boyi and the Four Haos' bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says Du Wei cultivated himself in reclusion, shunning office—almost in the mold of Boyi and the Four Haos.

sentences.zh: 周羣佔天有徵，杜瓊沈默慎密，諸生之純也。

translations.literal: Zhou Qun divined heaven with signs; Du Qiong sunk silent careful and close—among students the pure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qun’s astrology proved true; Du Qiong was silent and scrupulous—both were models of scholarly purity.

sentences.zh: 許、孟、來、李，博涉多聞，尹默精於左氏，雖不以德業為稱，信皆一時之學士。

translations.literal: Xu, Meng, Lai, Li—broadly waded much heard; Yin Mo refined in Zuo clan—although not by virtue and enterprise titled, truly all were one age's scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, Meng, Lai, and Li were widely read; Yin Mo mastered the Zuo commentary—though none were famed chiefly for moral achievement, all were leading scholars of their day.

sentences.zh: 譙周詞理淵通，為世碩儒，有董、揚之規，郤正文辭燦爛，有張、蔡之風，加其行止，君子有取焉。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou's wording and principle deep and thorough, was age's great Ru—had Dong and Yang's measure; Xi Zheng's literary phrasing brilliant splendor—had Zhang and Cai's wind; add their conduct and stopping—gentleman has what to take therein.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou’s learning ran deep like Dong Zhongshu or Yang Xiong; Xi Zheng’s prose shone in the manner of Zhang Heng and Cai Yong—and their conduct gives the gentleman much to approve.

sentences.zh: 二子處晉事少，在蜀事多，故著於篇。

translations.literal: The two sons' dwelling in Jin affairs few, in Shu affairs many—therefore set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Their careers in Jin were brief but their deeds in Shu were many, so they fill this chapter.

sentences.zh: 〈張璠以為譙周所陳降魏之策，蓋素料劉禪懦弱，心無害戾，故得行也。

translations.literal: 〈Zhang Fan thought Qiao Zhou's presented surrender Wei's strategy—probably always reckoned Liu Shan weak and timid, heart without harmful perversity—therefore was able to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan held that Qiao Zhou’s plan to surrender worked because he had long judged Liu Shan timid and harmless of heart.

sentences.zh: 如遇忿肆之人，雖無他算，然矜殉鄙恥，或發怒妄誅，以立一時之威，快其斯須之意者，此亦夷滅之禍云。〉

translations.literal: If meeting a wrathful unrestrained person—although no other scheme, yet priding on martyring base shame, or issuing anger reckless execution, to establish one moment's awe, satisfy his momentary intent—this also is extinction calamity.〉
translations.idiomatic: Had they faced a violent, touchy ruler with no larger design, pride and shame might have provoked random executions to assert a moment’s power—then utter ruin would have followed.〉
